   744→// Finalise finalises the state by removing the destructed objects and clears
   745→// the journal as well as the refunds. Finalise, however, will not push any updates
   746→// into the tries just yet. Only IntermediateRoot or Commit will do that.
   747→func (s *StateDB) Finalise(deleteEmptyObjects bool) {
   748→	addressesToPrefetch := make([]common.Address, 0, len(s.journal.dirties))
   749→	for addr := range s.journal.dirties {
   750→		obj, exist := s.stateObjects[addr]
   751→		if !exist {
   752→			// ripeMD is 'touched' at block 1714175, in tx 0x1237f737031e40bcde4a8b7e717b2d15e3ecadfe49bb1bbc71ee9deb09c6fcf2
   753→			// That tx goes out of gas, and although the notion of 'touched' does not exist there, the
   754→			// touch-event will still be recorded in the journal. Since ripeMD is a special snowflake,
   755→			// it will persist in the journal even though the journal is reverted. In this special circumstance,
   756→			// it may exist in `s.journal.dirties` but not in `s.stateObjects`.
   757→			// Thus, we can safely ignore it here
   758→			continue
   759→		}
   760→		if obj.selfDestructed || (deleteEmptyObjects && obj.empty()) {
   761→			delete(s.stateObjects, obj.address)
   762→			s.markDelete(addr)
   763→			// We need to maintain account deletions explicitly (will remain
   764→			// set indefinitely). Note only the first occurred self-destruct
   765→			// event is tracked.
   766→			if _, ok := s.stateObjectsDestruct[obj.address]; !ok {
   767→				s.stateObjectsDestruct[obj.address] = obj
   768→			}
   769→		} else {
   770→			obj.finalise()
   771→			s.markUpdate(addr)
   772→		}
   773→		// At this point, also ship the address off to the precacher. The precacher
   774→		// will start loading tries, and when the change is eventually committed,
   775→		// the commit-phase will be a lot faster
   776→		addressesToPrefetch = append(addressesToPrefetch, addr) // Copy needed for closure
   777→	}
   778→	if s.prefetcher != nil && len(addressesToPrefetch) > 0 {
   779→		if err := s.prefetcher.prefetch(common.Hash{}, s.originalRoot, common.Address{}, addressesToPrefetch, nil, false); err != nil {
   780→			log.Error("Failed to prefetch addresses", "addresses", len(addressesToPrefetch), "err", err)
   781→		}
   782→	}
   783→	// Invalidate journal because reverting across transactions is not allowed.
   784→	s.clearJournalAndRefund()
   785→}
   786→
   787→// IntermediateRoot computes the current root hash of the state trie.
   788→// It is called in between transactions to get the root hash that
   789→// goes into transaction receipts.
   790→func (s *StateDB) IntermediateRoot(deleteEmptyObjects bool) common.Hash {
   791→	// Finalise all the dirty storage states and write them into the tries
   792→	s.Finalise(deleteEmptyObjects)
   793→
   794→	// Initialize the trie if it's not constructed yet. If the prefetch
   795→	// is enabled, the trie constructed below will be replaced by the
   796→	// prefetched one.
   797→	//
   798→	// This operation must be done before state object storage hashing,
   799→	// as it assumes the main trie is already loaded.
   800→	if s.trie == nil {
   801→		tr, err := s.db.OpenTrie(s.originalRoot)
   802→		if err != nil {
   803→			s.setError(err)
   804→			return common.Hash{}
   805→		}
   806→		s.trie = tr
   807→	}
   808→	// If there was a trie prefetcher operating, terminate it async so that the
   809→	// individual storage tries can be updated as soon as the disk load finishes.
   810→	if s.prefetcher != nil {
   811→		s.prefetcher.terminate(true)
   812→		defer func() {
   813→			s.prefetcher.report()
   814→			s.prefetcher = nil // Pre-byzantium, unset any used up prefetcher
   815→		}()
   816→	}
   817→	// Process all storage updates concurrently. The state object update root
   818→	// method will internally call a blocking trie fetch from the prefetcher,
   819→	// so there's no need to explicitly wait for the prefetchers to finish.
   820→	var (
   821→		start   = time.Now()
   822→		workers errgroup.Group
   823→	)
   824→	if s.db.TrieDB().IsVerkle() {
   825→		// Whilst MPT storage tries are independent, Verkle has one single trie
   826→		// for all the accounts and all the storage slots merged together. The
   827→		// former can thus be simply parallelized, but updating the latter will
   828→		// need concurrency support within the trie itself. That's a TODO for a
   829→		// later time.
   830→		workers.SetLimit(1)
   831→	}
   832→	for addr, op := range s.mutations {
   833→		if op.applied || op.isDelete() {
   834→			continue
   835→		}
   836→		obj := s.stateObjects[addr] // closure for the task runner below
   837→		workers.Go(func() error {
   838→			if s.db.TrieDB().IsVerkle() {
   839→				obj.updateTrie()
   840→			} else {
   841→				obj.updateRoot()
   842→
   843→				// If witness building is enabled and the state object has a trie,
   844→				// gather the witnesses for its specific storage trie
   845→				if s.witness != nil && obj.trie != nil {
   846→					s.witness.AddState(obj.trie.Witness())
   847→				}
   848→			}
   849→			return nil
   850→		})
   851→	}
   852→	// If witness building is enabled, gather all the read-only accesses.
   853→	// Skip witness collection in Verkle mode, they will be gathered
   854→	// together at the end.
   855→	if s.witness != nil && !s.db.TrieDB().IsVerkle() {
   856→		// Pull in anything that has been accessed before destruction
   857→		for _, obj := range s.stateObjectsDestruct {
   858→			// Skip any objects that haven't touched their storage
   859→			if len(obj.originStorage) == 0 {
   860→				continue
   861→			}
   862→			if trie := obj.getPrefetchedTrie(); trie != nil {
   863→				witness := trie.Witness()
   864→				s.witness.AddState(witness)
   865→				if s.witnessStats != nil {
   866→					s.witnessStats.Add(witness, obj.addrHash)
   867→				}
   868→			} else if obj.trie != nil {
   869→				witness := obj.trie.Witness()
   870→				s.witness.AddState(witness)
   871→				if s.witnessStats != nil {
   872→					s.witnessStats.Add(witness, obj.addrHash)
   873→				}
   874→			}
   875→		}
   876→		// Pull in only-read and non-destructed trie witnesses
   877→		for _, obj := range s.stateObjects {
   878→			// Skip any objects that have been updated
   879→			if _, ok := s.mutations[obj.address]; ok {
   880→				continue
   881→			}
   882→			// Skip any objects that haven't touched their storage
   883→			if len(obj.originStorage) == 0 {
   884→				continue
   885→			}
   886→			if trie := obj.getPrefetchedTrie(); trie != nil {
   887→				witness := trie.Witness()
   888→				s.witness.AddState(witness)
   889→				if s.witnessStats != nil {
   890→					s.witnessStats.Add(witness, obj.addrHash)
   891→				}
   892→			} else if obj.trie != nil {
   893→				witness := obj.trie.Witness()
   894→				s.witness.AddState(witness)
   895→				if s.witnessStats != nil {
   896→					s.witnessStats.Add(witness, obj.addrHash)
   897→				}
   898→			}
   899→		}
   900→	}
   901→	workers.Wait()
   902→	s.StorageUpdates += time.Since(start)
   903→
   904→	// Now we're about to start to write changes to the trie. The trie is so far
   905→	// _untouched_. We can check with the prefetcher, if it can give us a trie
   906→	// which has the same root, but also has some content loaded into it.
   907→	//
   908→	// Don't check prefetcher if verkle trie has been used. In the context of verkle,
   909→	// only a single trie is used for state hashing. Replacing a non-nil verkle tree
   910→	// here could result in losing uncommitted changes from storage.
   911→	start = time.Now()
   912→	if s.prefetcher != nil {
   913→		if trie := s.prefetcher.trie(common.Hash{}, s.originalRoot); trie == nil {
   914→			log.Error("Failed to retrieve account pre-fetcher trie")
   915→		} else {
   916→			s.trie = trie
   917→		}
   918→	}
   919→	// Perform updates before deletions.  This prevents resolution of unnecessary trie nodes
   920→	// in circumstances similar to the following:
   921→	//
   922→	// Consider nodes `A` and `B` who share the same full node parent `P` and have no other siblings.
   923→	// During the execution of a block:
   924→	// - `A` self-destructs,
   925→	// - `C` is created, and also shares the parent `P`.
   926→	// If the self-destruct is handled first, then `P` would be left with only one child, thus collapsed
   927→	// into a shortnode. This requires `B` to be resolved from disk.
   928→	// Whereas if the created node is handled first, then the collapse is avoided, and `B` is not resolved.
   929→	var (
   930→		usedAddrs    []common.Address
   931→		deletedAddrs []common.Address
   932→	)
   933→	for addr, op := range s.mutations {
   934→		if op.applied {
   935→			continue
   936→		}
   937→		op.applied = true
   938→
   939→		if op.isDelete() {
   940→			deletedAddrs = append(deletedAddrs, addr)
   941→		} else {
   942→			s.updateStateObject(s.stateObjects[addr])
   943→			s.AccountUpdated += 1
   944→		}
   945→		usedAddrs = append(usedAddrs, addr) // Copy needed for closure
   946→	}
   947→	for _, deletedAddr := range deletedAddrs {
   948→		s.deleteStateObject(deletedAddr)
   949→		s.AccountDeleted += 1
   950→	}
   951→	s.AccountUpdates += time.Since(start)
   952→
   953→	if s.prefetcher != nil {
   954→		s.prefetcher.used(common.Hash{}, s.originalRoot, usedAddrs, nil)
   955→	}
   956→	// Track the amount of time wasted on hashing the account trie
   957→	defer func(start time.Time) { s.AccountHashes += time.Since(start) }(time.Now())
   958→
   959→	hash := s.trie.Hash()
   960→
   961→	// If witness building is enabled, gather the account trie witness
   962→	if s.witness != nil {
   963→		witness := s.trie.Witness()
   964→		s.witness.AddState(witness)
   965→		if s.witnessStats != nil {
   966→			s.witnessStats.Add(witness, common.Hash{})
   967→		}
   968→	}
   969→	return hash
   970→}

   985→// fastDeleteStorage is the function that efficiently deletes the storage trie
   986→// of a specific account. It leverages the associated state snapshot for fast
   987→// storage iteration and constructs trie node deletion markers by creating
   988→// stack trie with iterated slots.
   989→func (s *StateDB) fastDeleteStorage(snaps *snapshot.Tree, addrHash common.Hash, root common.Hash) (map[common.Hash][]byte, map[common.Hash][]byte, *trienode.NodeSet, error) {
   990→	iter, err := snaps.StorageIterator(s.originalRoot, addrHash, common.Hash{})
   991→	if err != nil {
   992→		return nil, nil, nil, err
   993→	}
   994→	defer iter.Release()
   995→
   996→	var (
   997→		nodes          = trienode.NewNodeSet(addrHash) // the set for trie node mutations (value is nil)
   998→		storages       = make(map[common.Hash][]byte)  // the set for storage mutations (value is nil)
   999→		storageOrigins = make(map[common.Hash][]byte)  // the set for tracking the original value of slot
  1000→	)
  1001→	stack := trie.NewStackTrie(func(path []byte, hash common.Hash, blob []byte) {
  1002→		nodes.AddNode(path, trienode.NewDeletedWithPrev(blob))
  1003→	})
  1004→	for iter.Next() {
  1005→		slot := common.CopyBytes(iter.Slot())
  1006→		if err := iter.Error(); err != nil { // error might occur after Slot function
  1007→			return nil, nil, nil, err
  1008→		}
  1009→		key := iter.Hash()
  1010→		storages[key] = nil
  1011→		storageOrigins[key] = slot
  1012→
  1013→		if err := stack.Update(key.Bytes(), slot); err != nil {
  1014→			return nil, nil, nil, err
  1015→		}
  1016→	}
  1017→	if err := iter.Error(); err != nil { // error might occur during iteration
  1018→		return nil, nil, nil, err
  1019→	}
  1020→	if stack.Hash() != root {
  1021→		return nil, nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("snapshot is not matched, exp %x, got %x", root, stack.Hash())
  1022→	}
  1023→	return storages, storageOrigins, nodes, nil
  1024→}

  1026→// slowDeleteStorage serves as a less-efficient alternative to "fastDeleteStorage,"
  1027→// employed when the associated state snapshot is not available. It iterates the
  1028→// storage slots along with all internal trie nodes via trie directly.
  1029→func (s *StateDB) slowDeleteStorage(addr common.Address, addrHash common.Hash, root common.Hash) (map[common.Hash][]byte, map[common.Hash][]byte, *trienode.NodeSet, error) {
  1030→	tr, err := s.db.OpenStorageTrie(s.originalRoot, addr, root, s.trie)
  1031→	if err != nil {
  1032→		return nil, nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to open storage trie, err: %w", err)
  1033→	}
  1034→	it, err := tr.NodeIterator(nil)
  1035→	if err != nil {
  1036→		return nil, nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to open storage iterator, err: %w", err)
  1037→	}
  1038→	var (
  1039→		nodes          = trienode.NewNodeSet(addrHash) // the set for trie node mutations (value is nil)
  1040→		storages       = make(map[common.Hash][]byte)  // the set for storage mutations (value is nil)
  1041→		storageOrigins = make(map[common.Hash][]byte)  // the set for tracking the original value of slot
  1042→	)
  1043→	for it.Next(true) {
  1044→		if it.Leaf() {
  1045→			key := common.BytesToHash(it.LeafKey())
  1046→			storages[key] = nil
  1047→			storageOrigins[key] = common.CopyBytes(it.LeafBlob())
  1048→			continue
  1049→		}
  1050→		if it.Hash() == (common.Hash{}) {
  1051→			continue
  1052→		}
  1053→		nodes.AddNode(it.Path(), trienode.NewDeletedWithPrev(it.NodeBlob()))
  1054→	}
  1055→	if err := it.Error(); err != nil {
  1056→		return nil, nil, nil, err
  1057→	}
  1058→	return storages, storageOrigins, nodes, nil
  1059→}

  1061→// deleteStorage is designed to delete the storage trie of a designated account.
  1062→// The function will make an attempt to utilize an efficient strategy if the
  1063→// associated state snapshot is reachable; otherwise, it will resort to a less
  1064→// efficient approach.
  1065→func (s *StateDB) deleteStorage(addr common.Address, addrHash common.Hash, root common.Hash) (map[common.Hash][]byte, map[common.Hash][]byte, *trienode.NodeSet, error) {
  1066→	var (
  1067→		err            error
  1068→		nodes          *trienode.NodeSet      // the set for trie node mutations (value is nil)
  1069→		storages       map[common.Hash][]byte // the set for storage mutations (value is nil)
  1070→		storageOrigins map[common.Hash][]byte // the set for tracking the original value of slot
  1071→	)
  1072→	// The fast approach can be failed if the snapshot is not fully
  1073→	// generated, or it's internally corrupted. Fallback to the slow
  1074→	// one just in case.
  1075→	snaps := s.db.Snapshot()
  1076→	if snaps != nil {
  1077→		storages, storageOrigins, nodes, err = s.fastDeleteStorage(snaps, addrHash, root)
  1078→	}
  1079→	if snaps == nil || err != nil {
  1080→		storages, storageOrigins, nodes, err = s.slowDeleteStorage(addr, addrHash, root)
  1081→	}
  1082→	if err != nil {
  1083→		return nil, nil, nil, err
  1084→	}
  1085→	return storages, storageOrigins, nodes, nil
  1086→}

  1088→// handleDestruction processes all destruction markers and deletes the account
  1089→// and associated storage slots if necessary. There are four potential scenarios
  1090→// as following:
  1091→//
  1092→//	(a) the account was not existent and be marked as destructed
  1093→//	(b) the account was not existent and be marked as destructed,
  1094→//	    however, it's resurrected later in the same block.
  1095→//	(c) the account was existent and be marked as destructed
  1096→//	(d) the account was existent and be marked as destructed,
  1097→//	    however it's resurrected later in the same block.
  1098→//
  1099→// In case (a), nothing needs be deleted, nil to nil transition can be ignored.
  1100→// In case (b), nothing needs be deleted, nil is used as the original value for
  1101→// newly created account and storages
  1102→// In case (c), **original** account along with its storages should be deleted,
  1103→// with their values be tracked as original value.
  1104→// In case (d), **original** account along with its storages should be deleted,
  1105→// with their values be tracked as original value.
  1106→func (s *StateDB) handleDestruction(noStorageWiping bool) (map[common.Hash]*accountDelete, []*trienode.NodeSet, error) {
  1107→	var (
  1108→		nodes   []*trienode.NodeSet
  1109→		deletes = make(map[common.Hash]*accountDelete)
  1110→	)
  1111→	for addr, prevObj := range s.stateObjectsDestruct {
  1112→		prev := prevObj.origin
  1113→
  1114→		// The account was non-existent, and it's marked as destructed in the scope
  1115→		// of block. It can be either case (a) or (b) and will be interpreted as
  1116→		// null->null state transition.
  1117→		// - for (a), skip it without doing anything
  1118→		// - for (b), the resurrected account with nil as original will be handled afterwards
  1119→		if prev == nil {
  1120→			continue
  1121→		}
  1122→		// The account was existent, it can be either case (c) or (d).
  1123→		addrHash := crypto.Keccak256Hash(addr.Bytes())
  1124→		op := &accountDelete{
  1125→			address: addr,
  1126→			origin:  types.SlimAccountRLP(*prev),
  1127→		}
  1128→		deletes[addrHash] = op
  1129→
  1130→		// Short circuit if the origin storage was empty.
  1131→		if prev.Root == types.EmptyRootHash || s.db.TrieDB().IsVerkle() {
  1132→			continue
  1133→		}
  1134→		if noStorageWiping {
  1135→			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("unexpected storage wiping, %x", addr)
  1136→		}
  1137→		// Remove storage slots belonging to the account.
  1138→		storages, storagesOrigin, set, err := s.deleteStorage(addr, addrHash, prev.Root)
  1139→		if err != nil {
  1140→			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to delete storage, err: %w", err)
  1141→		}
  1142→		op.storages = storages
  1143→		op.storagesOrigin = storagesOrigin
  1144→
  1145→		// Aggregate the associated trie node changes.
  1146→		nodes = append(nodes, set)
  1147→	}
  1148→	return deletes, nodes, nil
  1149→}

  1156→// commit gathers the state mutations accumulated along with the associated
  1157→// trie changes, resetting all internal flags with the new state as the base.
  1158→func (s *StateDB) commit(deleteEmptyObjects bool, noStorageWiping bool, blockNumber uint64) (*stateUpdate, error) {
  1159→	// Short circuit in case any database failure occurred earlier.
  1160→	if s.dbErr != nil {
  1161→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("commit aborted due to earlier error: %v", s.dbErr)
  1162→	}
  1163→	// Finalize any pending changes and merge everything into the tries
  1164→	s.IntermediateRoot(deleteEmptyObjects)
  1165→
  1166→	// Short circuit if any error occurs within the IntermediateRoot.
  1167→	if s.dbErr != nil {
  1168→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("commit aborted due to database error: %v", s.dbErr)
  1169→	}
  1170→	// Commit objects to the trie, measuring the elapsed time
  1171→	var (
  1172→		accountTrieNodesUpdated int
  1173→		accountTrieNodesDeleted int
  1174→		storageTrieNodesUpdated int
  1175→		storageTrieNodesDeleted int
  1176→
  1177→		lock    sync.Mutex                                               // protect two maps below
  1178→		nodes   = trienode.NewMergedNodeSet()                            // aggregated trie nodes
  1179→		updates = make(map[common.Hash]*accountUpdate, len(s.mutations)) // aggregated account updates
  1180→
  1181→		// merge aggregates the dirty trie nodes into the global set.
  1182→		//
  1183→		// Given that some accounts may be destroyed and then recreated within
  1184→		// the same block, it's possible that a node set with the same owner
  1185→		// may already exist. In such cases, these two sets are combined, with
  1186→		// the later one overwriting the previous one if any nodes are modified
  1187→		// or deleted in both sets.
  1188→		//
  1189→		// merge run concurrently across  all the state objects and account trie.
  1190→		merge = func(set *trienode.NodeSet) error {
  1191→			if set == nil {
  1192→				return nil
  1193→			}
  1194→			lock.Lock()
  1195→			defer lock.Unlock()
  1196→
  1197→			updates, deletes := set.Size()
  1198→			if set.Owner == (common.Hash{}) {
  1199→				accountTrieNodesUpdated += updates
  1200→				accountTrieNodesDeleted += deletes
  1201→			} else {
  1202→				storageTrieNodesUpdated += updates
  1203→				storageTrieNodesDeleted += deletes
  1204→			}
  1205→			return nodes.Merge(set)
  1206→		}
  1207→	)
  1208→	// Given that some accounts could be destroyed and then recreated within
  1209→	// the same block, account deletions must be processed first. This ensures
  1210→	// that the storage trie nodes deleted during destruction and recreated
  1211→	// during subsequent resurrection can be combined correctly.
  1212→	deletes, delNodes, err := s.handleDestruction(noStorageWiping)
  1213→	if err != nil {
  1214→		return nil, err
  1215→	}
  1216→	for _, set := range delNodes {
  1217→		if err := merge(set); err != nil {
  1218→			return nil, err
  1219→		}
  1220→	}
  1221→	// Handle all state updates afterwards, concurrently to one another to shave
  1222→	// off some milliseconds from the commit operation. Also accumulate the code
  1223→	// writes to run in parallel with the computations.
  1224→	var (
  1225→		start   = time.Now()
  1226→		root    common.Hash
  1227→		workers errgroup.Group
  1228→	)
  1229→	// Schedule the account trie first since that will be the biggest, so give
  1230→	// it the most time to crunch.
  1231→	//
  1232→	// TODO(karalabe): This account trie commit is *very* heavy. 5-6ms at chain
  1233→	// heads, which seems excessive given that it doesn't do hashing, it just
  1234→	// shuffles some data. For comparison, the *hashing* at chain head is 2-3ms.
  1235→	// We need to investigate what's happening as it seems something's wonky.
  1236→	// Obviously it's not an end of the world issue, just something the original
  1237→	// code didn't anticipate for.
  1238→	workers.Go(func() error {
  1239→		// Write the account trie changes, measuring the amount of wasted time
  1240→		newroot, set := s.trie.Commit(true)
  1241→		root = newroot
  1242→
  1243→		if err := merge(set); err != nil {
  1244→			return err
  1245→		}
  1246→		s.AccountCommits = time.Since(start)
  1247→		return nil
  1248→	})
  1249→	// Schedule each of the storage tries that need to be updated, so they can
  1250→	// run concurrently to one another.
  1251→	//
  1252→	// TODO(karalabe): Experimentally, the account commit takes approximately the
  1253→	// same time as all the storage commits combined, so we could maybe only have
  1254→	// 2 threads in total. But that kind of depends on the account commit being
  1255→	// more expensive than it should be, so let's fix that and revisit this todo.
  1256→	for addr, op := range s.mutations {
  1257→		if op.isDelete() {
  1258→			continue
  1259→		}
  1260→		// Write any contract code associated with the state object
  1261→		obj := s.stateObjects[addr]
  1262→		if obj == nil {
  1263→			return nil, errors.New("missing state object")
  1264→		}
  1265→		// Run the storage updates concurrently to one another
  1266→		workers.Go(func() error {
  1267→			// Write any storage changes in the state object to its storage trie
  1268→			update, set, err := obj.commit()
  1269→			if err != nil {
  1270→				return err
  1271→			}
  1272→			if err := merge(set); err != nil {
  1273→				return err
  1274→			}
  1275→			lock.Lock()
  1276→			updates[obj.addrHash] = update
  1277→			s.StorageCommits = time.Since(start) // overwrite with the longest storage commit runtime
  1278→			lock.Unlock()
  1279→			return nil
  1280→		})
  1281→	}
  1282→	// Wait for everything to finish and update the metrics
  1283→	if err := workers.Wait(); err != nil {
  1284→		return nil, err
  1285→	}
  1286→	accountReadMeters.Mark(int64(s.AccountLoaded))
  1287→	storageReadMeters.Mark(int64(s.StorageLoaded))
  1288→	accountUpdatedMeter.Mark(int64(s.AccountUpdated))
  1289→	storageUpdatedMeter.Mark(s.StorageUpdated.Load())
  1290→	accountDeletedMeter.Mark(int64(s.AccountDeleted))
  1291→	storageDeletedMeter.Mark(s.StorageDeleted.Load())
  1292→	accountTrieUpdatedMeter.Mark(int64(accountTrieNodesUpdated))
  1293→	accountTrieDeletedMeter.Mark(int64(accountTrieNodesDeleted))
  1294→	storageTriesUpdatedMeter.Mark(int64(storageTrieNodesUpdated))
  1295→	storageTriesDeletedMeter.Mark(int64(storageTrieNodesDeleted))
  1296→
  1297→	// Clear the metric markers
  1298→	s.AccountLoaded, s.AccountUpdated, s.AccountDeleted = 0, 0, 0
  1299→	s.StorageLoaded = 0
  1300→	s.StorageUpdated.Store(0)
  1301→	s.StorageDeleted.Store(0)
  1302→
  1303→	// Clear all internal flags and update state root at the end.
  1304→	s.mutations = make(map[common.Address]*mutation)
  1305→	s.stateObjectsDestruct = make(map[common.Address]*stateObject)
  1306→
  1307→	origin := s.originalRoot
  1308→	s.originalRoot = root

  1313→// commitAndFlush is a wrapper of commit which also commits the state mutations
  1314→// to the configured data stores.
  1315→func (s *StateDB) commitAndFlush(block uint64, deleteEmptyObjects bool, noStorageWiping bool) (*stateUpdate, error) {
  1316→	ret, err := s.commit(deleteEmptyObjects, noStorageWiping, block)
  1317→	if err != nil {
  1318→		return nil, err
  1319→	}
  1320→	// Commit dirty contract code if any exists
  1321→	if db := s.db.TrieDB().Disk(); db != nil && len(ret.codes) > 0 {
  1322→		batch := db.NewBatch()
  1323→		for _, code := range ret.codes {
  1324→			rawdb.WriteCode(batch, code.hash, code.blob)
  1325→		}
  1326→		if err := batch.Write(); err != nil {
  1327→			return nil, err
  1328→		}
  1329→	}
  1330→	if !ret.empty() {
  1331→		// If snapshotting is enabled, update the snapshot tree with this new version
  1332→		if snap := s.db.Snapshot(); snap != nil && snap.Snapshot(ret.originRoot) != nil {
  1333→			start := time.Now()
  1334→			if err := snap.Update(ret.root, ret.originRoot, ret.accounts, ret.storages); err != nil {
  1335→				log.Warn("Failed to update snapshot tree", "from", ret.originRoot, "to", ret.root, "err", err)
  1336→			}
  1337→			// Keep 128 diff layers in the memory, persistent layer is 129th.
  1338→			// - head layer is paired with HEAD state
  1339→			// - head-1 layer is paired with HEAD-1 state
  1340→			// - head-127 layer(bottom-most diff layer) is paired with HEAD-127 state
  1341→			if err := snap.Cap(ret.root, TriesInMemory); err != nil {
  1342→				log.Warn("Failed to cap snapshot tree", "root", ret.root, "layers", TriesInMemory, "err", err)
  1343→			}
  1344→			s.SnapshotCommits += time.Since(start)
  1345→		}
  1346→		// If trie database is enabled, commit the state update as a new layer
  1347→		if db := s.db.TrieDB(); db != nil {
  1348→			start := time.Now()
  1349→			if err := db.Update(ret.root, ret.originRoot, block, ret.nodes, ret.stateSet()); err != nil {
  1350→				return nil, err
  1351→			}
  1352→			s.TrieDBCommits += time.Since(start)
  1353→		}
  1354→	}
  1355→	s.reader, _ = s.db.Reader(s.originalRoot)
  1356→	return ret, err
  1357→}

  1359→// Commit writes the state mutations into the configured data stores.
  1360→//
  1361→// Once the state is committed, tries cached in stateDB (including account
  1362→// trie, storage tries) will no longer be functional. A new state instance
  1363→// must be created with new root and updated database for accessing post-
  1364→// commit states.

  1367→// for more chain context.

  1370→// Since self-destruction was deprecated with the Cancun fork and there are
  1371→// no empty accounts left that could be deleted by EIP-158, storage wiping
  1372→// should not occur.
  1373→func (s *StateDB) Commit(block uint64, deleteEmptyObjects bool, noStorageWiping bool) (common.Hash, error) {
  1374→	ret, err := s.commitAndFlush(block, deleteEmptyObjects, noStorageWiping)
  1375→	if err != nil {
  1376→		return common.Hash{}, err
  1377→	}
  1378→	return ret.root, nil

  1382→// This is useful for tracking state changes at the blockchain level.

  1385→	if err != nil {
  1386→		return common.Hash{}, nil, err
  1387→	}
  1388→	return ret.root, ret, nil

  1391→// Prepare handles the preparatory steps for executing a state transition with.
  1392→// This method must be invoked before state transition.
  1393→//
  1394→// Berlin fork:
  1395→// - Add sender to access list (2929)
  1396→// - Add destination to access list (2929)
  1397→// - Add precompiles to access list (2929)
  1398→// - Add the contents of the optional tx access list (2930)
  1399→//
  1400→// Potential EIPs:
  1401→// - Reset access list (Berlin)
  1402→// - Add coinbase to access list (EIP-3651)
  1403→// - Reset transient storage (EIP-1153)
  1404→func (s *StateDB) Prepare(rules params.Rules, sender, coinbase common.Address, dst *common.Address, precompiles []common.Address, list types.AccessList) {
  1405→	if rules.IsEIP2929 && rules.IsEIP4762 {
  1406→		panic("eip2929 and eip4762 are both activated")
  1407→	}
  1408→	if rules.IsEIP2929 {
  1409→		// Clear out any leftover from previous executions
  1410→		al := newAccessList()
  1411→		s.accessList = al
  1412→
  1413→		al.AddAddress(sender)
  1414→		if dst != nil {
  1415→			al.AddAddress(*dst)
  1416→			// If it's a create-tx, the destination will be added inside evm.create
  1417→		}
  1418→		for _, addr := range precompiles {
  1419→			al.AddAddress(addr)
  1420→		}
  1421→		for _, el := range list {
  1422→			al.AddAddress(el.Address)
  1423→			for _, key := range el.StorageKeys {
  1424→				al.AddSlot(el.Address, key)
  1425→			}
  1426→		}
  1427→		if rules.IsShanghai { // EIP-3651: warm coinbase
  1428→			al.AddAddress(coinbase)
  1429→		}
  1430→	}
  1431→	// Reset transient storage at the beginning of transaction execution
  1432→	s.transientStorage = newTransientStorage()
  1433→}

    36→// Set sets the transient-storage `value` for `key` at the given `addr`.
    37→func (t transientStorage) Set(addr common.Address, key, value common.Hash) {
    38→	if value == (common.Hash{}) { // this is a 'delete'
    39→		if _, ok := t[addr]; ok {

    41→			if len(t[addr]) == 0 {

    43→			}
    44→		}
    45→	} else {
    46→		if _, ok := t[addr]; !ok {
    47→			t[addr] = make(Storage)
    48→		}
    49→		t[addr][key] = value
    50→	}

    70→// IntrinsicGas computes the 'intrinsic gas' for a message with the given data.
    71→func IntrinsicGas(data []byte, accessList types.AccessList, authList []types.SetCodeAuthorization, isContractCreation, isHomestead, isEIP2028, isEIP3860 bool) (uint64, error) {

    73→	var gas uint64
    74→	if isContractCreation && isHomestead {
    75→		gas = params.TxGasContractCreation
    76→	} else {
    77→		gas = params.TxGas

    79→	dataLen := uint64(len(data))

    83→		z := uint64(bytes.Count(data, []byte{0}))
    84→		nz := dataLen - z
    85→
    86→		// Make sure we don't exceed uint64 for all data combinations
    87→		nonZeroGas := params.TxDataNonZeroGasFrontier
    88→		if isEIP2028 {
    89→			nonZeroGas = params.TxDataNonZeroGasEIP2028
    90→		}
    91→		if (math.MaxUint64-gas)/nonZeroGas < nz {
    92→			return 0, ErrGasUintOverflow
    93→		}
    94→		gas += nz * nonZeroGas
    95→
    96→		if (math.MaxUint64-gas)/params.TxDataZeroGas < z {
    97→			return 0, ErrGasUintOverflow
    98→		}
    99→		gas += z * params.TxDataZeroGas
   100→
   101→		if isContractCreation && isEIP3860 {
   102→			lenWords := toWordSize(dataLen)
   103→			if (math.MaxUint64-gas)/params.InitCodeWordGas < lenWords {
   104→				return 0, ErrGasUintOverflow
   105→			}
   106→			gas += lenWords * params.InitCodeWordGas
   107→		}
   108→	}
   109→	if accessList != nil {
   110→		gas += uint64(len(accessList)) * params.TxAccessListAddressGas
   111→		gas += uint64(accessList.StorageKeys()) * params.TxAccessListStorageKeyGas
   112→	}
   113→	if authList != nil {
   114→		gas += uint64(len(authList)) * params.CallNewAccountGas
   115→	}
   116→	return gas, nil
   117→}
   118→
   119→// FloorDataGas computes the minimum gas required for a transaction based on its data tokens (EIP-7623).
   120→func FloorDataGas(data []byte) (uint64, error) {
   121→	var (
   122→		z      = uint64(bytes.Count(data, []byte{0}))
   123→		nz     = uint64(len(data)) - z
   124→		tokens = nz*params.TxTokenPerNonZeroByte + z
   125→	)
   126→	// Check for overflow
   127→	if (math.MaxUint64-params.TxGas)/params.TxCostFloorPerToken < tokens {
   128→		return 0, ErrGasUintOverflow
   129→	}
   130→	// Minimum gas required for a transaction based on its data tokens (EIP-7623).
   131→	return params.TxGas + tokens*params.TxCostFloorPerToken, nil
   132→}
   133→
   134→// toWordSize returns the ceiled word size required for init code payment calculation.
   135→func toWordSize(size uint64) uint64 {
   136→	if size > math.MaxUint64-31 {
   137→		return math.MaxUint64/32 + 1
   138→	}
   139→
   140→	return (size + 31) / 32
   141→}

   143→// A Message contains the data derived from a single transaction that is relevant to state
   144→// processing.
   145→type Message struct {
   146→	To                    *common.Address
   147→	From                  common.Address
   148→	Nonce                 uint64
   149→	Value                 *big.Int
   150→	GasLimit              uint64
   151→	GasPrice              *big.Int
   152→	GasFeeCap             *big.Int
   153→	GasTipCap             *big.Int
   154→	Data                  []byte
   155→	AccessList            types.AccessList
   156→	BlobGasFeeCap         *big.Int
   157→	BlobHashes            []common.Hash
   158→	SetCodeAuthorizations []types.SetCodeAuthorization
   159→
   160→	// When SkipNonceChecks is true, the message nonce is not checked against the
   161→	// account nonce in state.
   162→	//
   163→	// This field will be set to true for operations like RPC eth_call
   164→	// or the state prefetching.
   165→	SkipNonceChecks bool
   166→
   167→	// When SkipFromEOACheck is true, the message sender is not checked to be an EOA.
   168→	SkipFromEOACheck bool
   169→}
   170→
   171→// TransactionToMessage converts a transaction into a Message.
   172→func TransactionToMessage(tx *types.Transaction, s types.Signer, baseFee *big.Int) (*Message, error) {
   173→	msg := &Message{
   174→		Nonce:                 tx.Nonce(),
   175→		GasLimit:              tx.Gas(),
   176→		GasPrice:              new(big.Int).Set(tx.GasPrice()),
   177→		GasFeeCap:             new(big.Int).Set(tx.GasFeeCap()),
   178→		GasTipCap:             new(big.Int).Set(tx.GasTipCap()),
   179→		To:                    tx.To(),
   180→		Value:                 tx.Value(),
   181→		Data:                  tx.Data(),
   182→		AccessList:            tx.AccessList(),
   183→		SetCodeAuthorizations: tx.SetCodeAuthorizations(),
   184→		SkipNonceChecks:       false,
   185→		SkipFromEOACheck:      false,
   186→		BlobHashes:            tx.BlobHashes(),
   187→		BlobGasFeeCap:         tx.BlobGasFeeCap(),
   188→	}
   189→	// If baseFee provided, set gasPrice to effectiveGasPrice.
   190→	if baseFee != nil {
   191→		msg.GasPrice = msg.GasPrice.Add(msg.GasTipCap, baseFee)
   192→		if msg.GasPrice.Cmp(msg.GasFeeCap) > 0 {
   193→			msg.GasPrice = msg.GasFeeCap
   194→		}
   195→	}
   196→	var err error
   197→	msg.From, err = types.Sender(s, tx)
   198→	return msg, err
   199→}

   201→// ApplyMessage computes the new state by applying the given message
   202→// against the old state within the environment.
   203→//
   204→// ApplyMessage returns the bytes returned by any EVM execution (if it took place),
   205→// the gas used (which includes gas refunds) and an error if it failed. An error always
   206→// indicates a core error meaning that the message would always fail for that particular
   207→// state and would never be accepted within a block.
   208→func ApplyMessage(evm *vm.EVM, msg *Message, gp *GasPool) (*ExecutionResult, error) {
   209→	evm.SetTxContext(NewEVMTxContext(msg))
   210→	return newStateTransition(evm, msg, gp).execute()
   211→}
   212→
   213→// stateTransition represents a state transition.
   214→//
   215→// == The State Transitioning Model
   216→//
   217→// A state transition is a change made when a transaction is applied to the current world
   218→// state. The state transitioning model does all the necessary work to work out a valid new
   219→// state root.
   220→//
   221→//  1. Nonce handling
   222→//  2. Pre pay gas
   223→//  3. Create a new state object if the recipient is nil
   224→//  4. Value transfer
   225→//
   226→// == If contract creation ==
   227→//
   228→//	4a. Attempt to run transaction data
   229→//	4b. If valid, use result as code for the new state object
   230→//
   231→// == end ==
   232→//
   233→//  5. Run Script section
   234→//  6. Derive new state root
   235→type stateTransition struct {
   236→	gp           *GasPool
   237→	msg          *Message
   238→	gasRemaining uint64
   239→	initialGas   uint64
   240→	state        vm.StateDB
   241→	evm          *vm.EVM
   242→}
   243→
   244→// newStateTransition initialises and returns a new state transition object.
   245→func newStateTransition(evm *vm.EVM, msg *Message, gp *GasPool) *stateTransition {
   246→	return &stateTransition{
   247→		gp:    gp,
   248→		evm:   evm,
   249→		msg:   msg,
   250→		state: evm.StateDB,
   251→	}
   252→}
   253→
   254→// to returns the recipient of the message.
   255→func (st *stateTransition) to() common.Address {
   256→	if st.msg == nil || st.msg.To == nil /* contract creation */ {
   257→		return common.Address{}
   258→	}
   259→	return *st.msg.To
   260→}

   262→func (st *stateTransition) buyGas() error {
   263→	mgval := new(big.Int).SetUint64(st.msg.GasLimit)
   264→	mgval.Mul(mgval, st.msg.GasPrice)
   265→	balanceCheck := new(big.Int).Set(mgval)
   266→	if st.msg.GasFeeCap != nil {
   267→		balanceCheck.SetUint64(st.msg.GasLimit)
   268→		balanceCheck = balanceCheck.Mul(balanceCheck, st.msg.GasFeeCap)
   269→	}
   270→	balanceCheck.Add(balanceCheck, st.msg.Value)
   271→
   272→	if st.evm.ChainConfig().IsCancun(st.evm.Context.BlockNumber, st.evm.Context.Time) {
   273→		if blobGas := st.blobGasUsed(); blobGas > 0 {
   274→			// Check that the user has enough funds to cover blobGasUsed * tx.BlobGasFeeCap
   275→			blobBalanceCheck := new(big.Int).SetUint64(blobGas)
   276→			blobBalanceCheck.Mul(blobBalanceCheck, st.msg.BlobGasFeeCap)
   277→			balanceCheck.Add(balanceCheck, blobBalanceCheck)
   278→			// Pay for blobGasUsed * actual blob fee
   279→			blobFee := new(big.Int).SetUint64(blobGas)
   280→			blobFee.Mul(blobFee, st.evm.Context.BlobBaseFee)
   281→			mgval.Add(mgval, blobFee)
   282→		}
   283→	}
   284→	balanceCheckU256, overflow := uint256.FromBig(balanceCheck)
   285→	if overflow {
   286→		return fmt.Errorf("%w: address %v required balance exceeds 256 bits", ErrInsufficientFunds, st.msg.From.Hex())
   287→	}
   288→	if have, want := st.state.GetBalance(st.msg.From), balanceCheckU256; have.Cmp(want) < 0 {
   289→		return fmt.Errorf("%w: address %v have %v want %v", ErrInsufficientFunds, st.msg.From.Hex(), have, want)
   290→	}
   291→	if err := st.gp.SubGas(st.msg.GasLimit); err != nil {
   292→		return err
   293→	}
   294→
   295→	if st.evm.Config.Tracer != nil && st.evm.Config.Tracer.OnGasChange != nil {
   296→		st.evm.Config.Tracer.OnGasChange(0, st.msg.GasLimit, tracing.GasChangeTxInitialBalance)
   297→	}
   298→	st.gasRemaining = st.msg.GasLimit
   299→
   300→	st.initialGas = st.msg.GasLimit
   301→	mgvalU256, _ := uint256.FromBig(mgval)
   302→	st.state.SubBalance(st.msg.From, mgvalU256, tracing.BalanceDecreaseGasBuy)
   303→	return nil
   304→}
   305→
   306→func (st *stateTransition) preCheck() error {
   307→	// Only check transactions that are not fake
   308→	msg := st.msg
   309→	if !msg.SkipNonceChecks {
   310→		// Make sure this transaction's nonce is correct.
   311→		stNonce := st.state.GetNonce(msg.From)
   312→		if msgNonce := msg.Nonce; stNonce < msgNonce {
   313→			return fmt.Errorf("%w: address %v, tx: %d state: %d", ErrNonceTooHigh,
   314→				msg.From.Hex(), msgNonce, stNonce)
   315→		} else if stNonce > msgNonce {
   316→			return fmt.Errorf("%w: address %v, tx: %d state: %d", ErrNonceTooLow,
   317→				msg.From.Hex(), msgNonce, stNonce)
   318→		} else if stNonce+1 < stNonce {
   319→			return fmt.Errorf("%w: address %v, nonce: %d", ErrNonceMax,
   320→				msg.From.Hex(), stNonce)
   321→		}
   322→	}
   323→	if !msg.SkipFromEOACheck {
   324→		// Make sure the sender is an EOA
   325→		code := st.state.GetCode(msg.From)
   326→		_, delegated := types.ParseDelegation(code)
   327→		if len(code) > 0 && !delegated {
   328→			return fmt.Errorf("%w: address %v, len(code): %d", ErrSenderNoEOA, msg.From.Hex(), len(code))
   329→		}
   330→	}
   331→	// Make sure that transaction gasFeeCap is greater than the baseFee (post london)
   332→	if st.evm.ChainConfig().IsLondon(st.evm.Context.BlockNumber) {
   333→		// Skip the checks if gas fields are zero and baseFee was explicitly disabled (eth_call)
   334→		skipCheck := st.evm.Config.NoBaseFee && msg.GasFeeCap.BitLen() == 0 && msg.GasTipCap.BitLen() == 0
   335→		if !skipCheck {
   336→			if l := msg.GasFeeCap.BitLen(); l > 256 {
   337→				return fmt.Errorf("%w: address %v, maxFeePerGas bit length: %d", ErrFeeCapVeryHigh,
   338→					msg.From.Hex(), l)
   339→			}
   340→			if l := msg.GasTipCap.BitLen(); l > 256 {
   341→				return fmt.Errorf("%w: address %v, maxPriorityFeePerGas bit length: %d", ErrTipVeryHigh,
   342→					msg.From.Hex(), l)
   343→			}
   344→			if msg.GasFeeCap.Cmp(msg.GasTipCap) < 0 {
   345→				return fmt.Errorf("%w: address %v, maxPriorityFeePerGas: %s, maxFeePerGas: %s", ErrTipAboveFeeCap,
   346→					msg.From.Hex(), msg.GasTipCap, msg.GasFeeCap)
   347→			}
   348→			// This will panic if baseFee is nil, but basefee presence is verified
   349→			// as part of header validation.
   350→			if msg.GasFeeCap.Cmp(st.evm.Context.BaseFee) < 0 {
   351→				return fmt.Errorf("%w: address %v, maxFeePerGas: %s, baseFee: %s", ErrFeeCapTooLow,
   352→					msg.From.Hex(), msg.GasFeeCap, st.evm.Context.BaseFee)
   353→			}
   354→		}
   355→	}
   356→	// Check the blob version validity
   357→	isOsaka := st.evm.ChainConfig().IsOsaka(st.evm.Context.BlockNumber, st.evm.Context.Time)
   358→	if msg.BlobHashes != nil {
   359→		// The to field of a blob tx type is mandatory, and a `BlobTx` transaction internally
   360→		// has it as a non-nillable value, so any msg derived from blob transaction has it non-nil.
   361→		// However, messages created through RPC (eth_call) don't have this restriction.
   362→		if msg.To == nil {
   363→			return ErrBlobTxCreate
   364→		}
   365→		if len(msg.BlobHashes) == 0 {
   366→			return ErrMissingBlobHashes
   367→		}
   368→		if isOsaka && len(msg.BlobHashes) > params.BlobTxMaxBlobs {
   369→			return ErrTooManyBlobs
   370→		}
   371→		for i, hash := range msg.BlobHashes {
   372→			if !kzg4844.IsValidVersionedHash(hash[:]) {
   373→				return fmt.Errorf("blob %d has invalid hash version", i)
   374→			}
   375→		}
   376→	}
   377→	// Check that the user is paying at least the current blob fee
   378→	if st.evm.ChainConfig().IsCancun(st.evm.Context.BlockNumber, st.evm.Context.Time) {
   379→		if st.blobGasUsed() > 0 {
   380→			// Skip the checks if gas fields are zero and blobBaseFee was explicitly disabled (eth_call)
   381→			skipCheck := st.evm.Config.NoBaseFee && msg.BlobGasFeeCap.BitLen() == 0
   382→			if !skipCheck {
   383→				// This will panic if blobBaseFee is nil, but blobBaseFee presence
   384→				// is verified as part of header validation.
   385→				if msg.BlobGasFeeCap.Cmp(st.evm.Context.BlobBaseFee) < 0 {
   386→					return fmt.Errorf("%w: address %v blobGasFeeCap: %v, blobBaseFee: %v", ErrBlobFeeCapTooLow,
   387→						msg.From.Hex(), msg.BlobGasFeeCap, st.evm.Context.BlobBaseFee)
   388→				}
   389→			}
   390→		}
   391→	}
   392→	// Check that EIP-7702 authorization list signatures are well formed.
   393→	if msg.SetCodeAuthorizations != nil {
   394→		if msg.To == nil {
   395→			return fmt.Errorf("%w (sender %v)", ErrSetCodeTxCreate, msg.From)
   396→		}
   397→		if len(msg.SetCodeAuthorizations) == 0 {
   398→			return fmt.Errorf("%w (sender %v)", ErrEmptyAuthList, msg.From)
   399→		}
   400→	}
   401→	// Verify tx gas limit does not exceed EIP-7825 cap.
   402→	if isOsaka && msg.GasLimit > params.MaxTxGas {
   403→		return fmt.Errorf("%w (cap: %d, tx: %d)", ErrGasLimitTooHigh, params.MaxTxGas, msg.GasLimit)
   404→	}
   405→	return st.buyGas()
   406→}
   407→
   408→// execute will transition the state by applying the current message and
   409→// returning the evm execution result with following fields.
   410→//
   411→//   - used gas: total gas used (including gas being refunded)
   412→//   - returndata: the returned data from evm
   413→//   - concrete execution error: various EVM errors which abort the execution, e.g.
   414→//     ErrOutOfGas, ErrExecutionReverted
   415→//
   416→// However if any consensus issue encountered, return the error directly with
   417→// nil evm execution result.
   418→func (st *stateTransition) execute() (*ExecutionResult, error) {
   419→	// First check this message satisfies all consensus rules before
   420→	// applying the message. The rules include these clauses
   421→	//
   422→	// 1. the nonce of the message caller is correct
   423→	// 2. caller has enough balance to cover transaction fee(gaslimit * gasprice)
   424→	// 3. the amount of gas required is available in the block
   425→	// 4. the purchased gas is enough to cover intrinsic usage
   426→	// 5. there is no overflow when calculating intrinsic gas
   427→	// 6. caller has enough balance to cover asset transfer for **topmost** call
   428→
   429→	// Check clauses 1-3, buy gas if everything is correct
   430→	if err := st.preCheck(); err != nil {
   431→		return nil, err
   432→	}
   433→
   434→	var (
   435→		msg              = st.msg
   436→		rules            = st.evm.ChainConfig().Rules(st.evm.Context.BlockNumber, st.evm.Context.Random != nil, st.evm.Context.Time)
   437→		contractCreation = msg.To == nil
   438→		floorDataGas     uint64
   439→	)
   440→
   441→	// Check clauses 4-5, subtract intrinsic gas if everything is correct
   442→	gas, err := IntrinsicGas(msg.Data, msg.AccessList, msg.SetCodeAuthorizations, contractCreation, rules.IsHomestead, rules.IsIstanbul, rules.IsShanghai)
   443→	if err != nil {
   444→		return nil, err
   445→	}
   446→	if st.gasRemaining < gas {
   447→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: have %d, want %d", ErrIntrinsicGas, st.gasRemaining, gas)
   448→	}
   449→	// Gas limit suffices for the floor data cost (EIP-7623)
   450→	if rules.IsPrague {
   451→		floorDataGas, err = FloorDataGas(msg.Data)
   452→		if err != nil {
   453→			return nil, err
   454→		}
   455→		if msg.GasLimit < floorDataGas {
   456→			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: have %d, want %d", ErrFloorDataGas, msg.GasLimit, floorDataGas)
   457→		}
   458→	}
   459→	if t := st.evm.Config.Tracer; t != nil && t.OnGasChange != nil {
   460→		t.OnGasChange(st.gasRemaining, st.gasRemaining-gas, tracing.GasChangeTxIntrinsicGas)
   461→	}
   462→	st.gasRemaining -= gas
   463→
   464→	if rules.IsEIP4762 {
   465→		st.evm.AccessEvents.AddTxOrigin(msg.From)
   466→
   467→		if targetAddr := msg.To; targetAddr != nil {
   468→			st.evm.AccessEvents.AddTxDestination(*targetAddr, msg.Value.Sign() != 0, !st.state.Exist(*targetAddr))
   469→		}
   470→	}
   471→
   472→	// Check clause 6
   473→	value, overflow := uint256.FromBig(msg.Value)
   474→	if overflow {
   475→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: address %v", ErrInsufficientFundsForTransfer, msg.From.Hex())
   476→	}
   477→	if !value.IsZero() && !st.evm.Context.CanTransfer(st.state, msg.From, value) {
   478→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: address %v", ErrInsufficientFundsForTransfer, msg.From.Hex())
   479→	}
   480→
   481→	// Check whether the init code size has been exceeded.
   482→	if rules.IsShanghai && contractCreation && len(msg.Data) > params.MaxInitCodeSize {
   483→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: code size %v limit %v", ErrMaxInitCodeSizeExceeded, len(msg.Data), params.MaxInitCodeSize)
   484→	}
   485→
   486→	// Execute the preparatory steps for state transition which includes:
   487→	// - prepare accessList(post-berlin)
   488→	// - reset transient storage(eip 1153)
   489→	st.state.Prepare(rules, msg.From, st.evm.Context.Coinbase, msg.To, vm.ActivePrecompiles(rules), msg.AccessList)
   490→
   491→	var (
   492→		ret   []byte
   493→		vmerr error // vm errors do not effect consensus and are therefore not assigned to err
   494→	)
   495→	if contractCreation {
   496→		ret, _, st.gasRemaining, vmerr = st.evm.Create(msg.From, msg.Data, st.gasRemaining, value)
   497→	} else {
   498→		// Increment the nonce for the next transaction.
   499→		st.state.SetNonce(msg.From, st.state.GetNonce(msg.From)+1, tracing.NonceChangeEoACall)
   500→
   501→		// Apply EIP-7702 authorizations.
   502→		if msg.SetCodeAuthorizations != nil {
   503→			for _, auth := range msg.SetCodeAuthorizations {
   504→				// Note errors are ignored, we simply skip invalid authorizations here.
   505→				st.applyAuthorization(&auth)
   506→			}
   507→		}
   508→
   509→		// Perform convenience warming of sender's delegation target. Although the
   510→		// sender is already warmed in Prepare(..), it's possible a delegation to
   511→		// the account was deployed during this transaction. To handle correctly,
   512→		// simply wait until the final state of delegations is determined before
   513→		// performing the resolution and warming.
   514→		if addr, ok := types.ParseDelegation(st.state.GetCode(*msg.To)); ok {
   515→			st.state.AddAddressToAccessList(addr)
   516→		}
   517→
   518→		// Execute the transaction's call.
   519→		ret, st.gasRemaining, vmerr = st.evm.Call(msg.From, st.to(), msg.Data, st.gasRemaining, value)
   520→	}
   521→
   522→	// Record the gas used excluding gas refunds. This value represents the actual
   523→	// gas allowance required to complete execution.
   524→	peakGasUsed := st.gasUsed()
   525→
   526→	// Compute refund counter, capped to a refund quotient.
   527→	st.gasRemaining += st.calcRefund()
   528→	if rules.IsPrague {
   529→		// After EIP-7623: Data-heavy transactions pay the floor gas.
   530→		if st.gasUsed() < floorDataGas {
   531→			prev := st.gasRemaining
   532→			st.gasRemaining = st.initialGas - floorDataGas
   533→			if t := st.evm.Config.Tracer; t != nil && t.OnGasChange != nil {
   534→				t.OnGasChange(prev, st.gasRemaining, tracing.GasChangeTxDataFloor)
   535→			}
   536→		}
   537→		if peakGasUsed < floorDataGas {
   538→			peakGasUsed = floorDataGas
   539→		}
   540→	}
   541→	st.returnGas()
   542→
   543→	effectiveTip := msg.GasPrice
   544→	if rules.IsLondon {
   545→		effectiveTip = new(big.Int).Sub(msg.GasPrice, st.evm.Context.BaseFee)
   546→	}
   547→	effectiveTipU256, _ := uint256.FromBig(effectiveTip)
   548→
   549→	if st.evm.Config.NoBaseFee && msg.GasFeeCap.Sign() == 0 && msg.GasTipCap.Sign() == 0 {
   550→		// Skip fee payment when NoBaseFee is set and the fee fields
   551→		// are 0. This avoids a negative effectiveTip being applied to
   552→		// the coinbase when simulating calls.
   553→	} else {
   554→		fee := new(uint256.Int).SetUint64(st.gasUsed())
   555→		fee.Mul(fee, effectiveTipU256)
   556→		st.state.AddBalance(st.evm.Context.Coinbase, fee, tracing.BalanceIncreaseRewardTransactionFee)
   557→
   558→		// add the coinbase to the witness iff the fee is greater than 0
   559→		if rules.IsEIP4762 && fee.Sign() != 0 {
   560→			st.evm.AccessEvents.AddAccount(st.evm.Context.Coinbase, true, math.MaxUint64)
   561→		}
   562→	}
   563→
   564→	return &ExecutionResult{
   565→		UsedGas:    st.gasUsed(),
   566→		MaxUsedGas: peakGasUsed,
   567→		Err:        vmerr,
   568→		ReturnData: ret,
   569→	}, nil
   570→}
   571→
   572→// validateAuthorization validates an EIP-7702 authorization against the state.
   573→func (st *stateTransition) validateAuthorization(auth *types.SetCodeAuthorization) (authority common.Address, err error) {
   574→	// Verify chain ID is null or equal to current chain ID.
   575→	if !auth.ChainID.IsZero() && auth.ChainID.CmpBig(st.evm.ChainConfig().ChainID) != 0 {
   576→		return authority, ErrAuthorizationWrongChainID
   577→	}
   578→	// Limit nonce to 2^64-1 per EIP-2681.
   579→	if auth.Nonce+1 < auth.Nonce {
   580→		return authority, ErrAuthorizationNonceOverflow
   581→	}
   582→	// Validate signature values and recover authority.
   583→	authority, err = auth.Authority()
   584→	if err != nil {
   585→		return authority, fmt.Errorf("%w: %v", ErrAuthorizationInvalidSignature, err)
   586→	}
   587→	// Check the authority account
   588→	//  1) doesn't have code or has exisiting delegation
   589→	//  2) matches the auth's nonce
   590→	//
   591→	// Note it is added to the access list even if the authorization is invalid.
   592→	st.state.AddAddressToAccessList(authority)
   593→	code := st.state.GetCode(authority)
   594→	if _, ok := types.ParseDelegation(code); len(code) != 0 && !ok {
   595→		return authority, ErrAuthorizationDestinationHasCode
   596→	}
   597→	if have := st.state.GetNonce(authority); have != auth.Nonce {
   598→		return authority, ErrAuthorizationNonceMismatch
   599→	}
   600→	return authority, nil
   601→}
   602→
   603→// applyAuthorization applies an EIP-7702 code delegation to the state.
   604→func (st *stateTransition) applyAuthorization(auth *types.SetCodeAuthorization) error {
   605→	authority, err := st.validateAuthorization(auth)
   606→	if err != nil {
   607→		return err
   608→	}
   609→
   610→	// If the account already exists in state, refund the new account cost
   611→	// charged in the intrinsic calculation.
   612→	if st.state.Exist(authority) {
   613→		st.state.AddRefund(params.CallNewAccountGas - params.TxAuthTupleGas)
   614→	}
   615→
   616→	// Update nonce and account code.
   617→	st.state.SetNonce(authority, auth.Nonce+1, tracing.NonceChangeAuthorization)
   618→	if auth.Address == (common.Address{}) {
   619→		// Delegation to zero address means clear.
   620→		st.state.SetCode(authority, nil, tracing.CodeChangeAuthorizationClear)
   621→		return nil
   622→	}
   623→
   624→	// Otherwise install delegation to auth.Address.
   625→	st.state.SetCode(authority, types.AddressToDelegation(auth.Address), tracing.CodeChangeAuthorization)
   626→
   627→	return nil
   628→}

   630→// calcRefund computes refund counter, capped to a refund quotient.
   631→func (st *stateTransition) calcRefund() uint64 {
   632→	var refund uint64
   633→	if !st.evm.ChainConfig().IsLondon(st.evm.Context.BlockNumber) {
   634→		// Before EIP-3529: refunds were capped to gasUsed / 2
   635→		refund = st.gasUsed() / params.RefundQuotient
   636→	} else {
   637→		// After EIP-3529: refunds are capped to gasUsed / 5
   638→		refund = st.gasUsed() / params.RefundQuotientEIP3529
   639→	}
   640→	if refund > st.state.GetRefund() {
   641→		refund = st.state.GetRefund()
   642→	}
   643→	if st.evm.Config.Tracer != nil && st.evm.Config.Tracer.OnGasChange != nil && refund > 0 {
   644→		st.evm.Config.Tracer.OnGasChange(st.gasRemaining, st.gasRemaining+refund, tracing.GasChangeTxRefunds)
   645→	}
   646→	return refund
   647→}

   649→// returnGas returns ETH for remaining gas,
   650→// exchanged at the original rate.
   651→func (st *stateTransition) returnGas() {
   652→	remaining := uint256.NewInt(st.gasRemaining)
   653→	remaining.Mul(remaining, uint256.MustFromBig(st.msg.GasPrice))
   654→	st.state.AddBalance(st.msg.From, remaining, tracing.BalanceIncreaseGasReturn)
   655→
   656→	if st.evm.Config.Tracer != nil && st.evm.Config.Tracer.OnGasChange != nil && st.gasRemaining > 0 {
   657→		st.evm.Config.Tracer.OnGasChange(st.gasRemaining, 0, tracing.GasChangeTxLeftOverReturned)
   658→	}
   659→
   660→	// Also return remaining gas to the block gas counter so it is
   661→	// available for the next transaction.
   662→	st.gp.AddGas(st.gasRemaining)
   663→}
   664→
   665→// gasUsed returns the amount of gas used up by the state transition.
   666→func (st *stateTransition) gasUsed() uint64 {
   667→	return st.initialGas - st.gasRemaining
   668→}

    86→	m.cacheMu.Unlock()
    87→}
    88→
    89→// Forward removes all transactions from the map with a nonce lower than the
    90→// provided threshold. Every removed transaction is returned for any post-removal
    91→// maintenance.
    92→func (m *SortedMap) Forward(threshold uint64) types.Transactions {
    93→	var removed types.Transactions
    94→
    95→	// Pop off heap items until the threshold is reached
    96→	for m.index.Len() > 0 && (*m.index)[0] < threshold {
    97→		nonce := heap.Pop(m.index).(uint64)
    98→		removed = append(removed, m.items[nonce])
    99→		delete(m.items, nonce)
   100→	}
   101→	// If we had a cached order, shift the front
   102→	m.cacheMu.Lock()
   103→	if m.cache != nil {
   104→		m.cache = m.cache[len(removed):]
   105→	}
   106→	m.cacheMu.Unlock()
   107→	return removed
   108→}
   109→
   110→// Filter iterates over the list of transactions and removes all of them for which
   111→// the specified function evaluates to true.
   112→// Filter, as opposed to 'filter', re-initialises the heap after the operation is done.
   113→// If you want to do several consecutive filterings, it's therefore better to first
   114→// do a .filter(func1) followed by .Filter(func2) or reheap()
   115→func (m *SortedMap) Filter(filter func(*types.Transaction) bool) types.Transactions {
   116→	removed := m.filter(filter)
   117→	// If transactions were removed, the heap and cache are ruined
   118→	if len(removed) > 0 {
   119→		m.reheap()
   120→	}
   121→	return removed
   122→}
   123→
   124→func (m *SortedMap) reheap() {
   125→	*m.index = make([]uint64, 0, len(m.items))
   126→	for nonce := range m.items {
   127→		*m.index = append(*m.index, nonce)
   128→	}
   129→	heap.Init(m.index)
   130→	m.cacheMu.Lock()
   131→	m.cache = nil
   132→	m.cacheMu.Unlock()
   133→}
   134→
   135→// filter is identical to Filter, but **does not** regenerate the heap. This method
   136→// should only be used if followed immediately by a call to Filter or reheap()
   137→func (m *SortedMap) filter(filter func(*types.Transaction) bool) types.Transactions {
   138→	var removed types.Transactions
   139→
   140→	// Collect all the transactions to filter out
   141→	for nonce, tx := range m.items {
   142→		if filter(tx) {
   143→			removed = append(removed, tx)
   144→			delete(m.items, nonce)
   145→		}
   146→	}
   147→	if len(removed) > 0 {
   148→		m.cacheMu.Lock()
   149→		m.cache = nil
   150→		m.cacheMu.Unlock()
   151→	}
   152→	return removed
   153→}
   154→
   155→// Cap places a hard limit on the number of items, returning all transactions
   156→// exceeding that limit.
   157→func (m *SortedMap) Cap(threshold int) types.Transactions {
   158→	// Short circuit if the number of items is under the limit
   159→	if len(m.items) <= threshold {
   160→		return nil
   161→	}
   162→	// Otherwise gather and drop the highest nonce'd transactions
   163→	var drops types.Transactions
   164→	slices.Sort(*m.index)
   165→	for size := len(m.items); size > threshold; size-- {
   166→		drops = append(drops, m.items[(*m.index)[size-1]])
   167→		delete(m.items, (*m.index)[size-1])
   168→	}
   169→	*m.index = (*m.index)[:threshold]
   170→	// The sorted m.index slice is still a valid heap, so there is no need to
   171→	// reheap after deleting tail items.
   172→
   173→	// If we had a cache, shift the back
   174→	m.cacheMu.Lock()
   175→	if m.cache != nil {
   176→		m.cache = m.cache[:len(m.cache)-len(drops)]
   177→	}
   178→	m.cacheMu.Unlock()
   179→	return drops
   180→}
   181→
   182→// Remove deletes a transaction from the maintained map, returning whether the
   183→// transaction was found.
   184→func (m *SortedMap) Remove(nonce uint64) bool {
   185→	// Short circuit if no transaction is present
   186→	_, ok := m.items[nonce]
   187→	if !ok {
   188→		return false
   189→	}
   190→	// Otherwise delete the transaction and fix the heap index
   191→	for i := 0; i < m.index.Len(); i++ {
   192→		if (*m.index)[i] == nonce {
   193→			heap.Remove(m.index, i)
   194→			break
   195→		}
   196→	}
   197→	delete(m.items, nonce)
   198→	m.cacheMu.Lock()
   199→	m.cache = nil
   200→	m.cacheMu.Unlock()
   201→
   202→	return true
   203→}
   204→
   205→// Ready retrieves a sequentially increasing list of transactions starting at the
   206→// provided nonce that is ready for processing. The returned transactions will be
   207→// removed from the list.
   208→//
   209→// Note, all transactions with nonces lower than start will also be returned to
   210→// prevent getting into an invalid state. This is not something that should ever
   211→// happen but better to be self correcting than failing!
   212→func (m *SortedMap) Ready(start uint64) types.Transactions {
   213→	// Short circuit if no transactions are available
   214→	if m.index.Len() == 0 || (*m.index)[0] > start {
   215→		return nil
   216→	}
   217→	// Otherwise start accumulating incremental transactions
   218→	var ready types.Transactions
   219→	for next := (*m.index)[0]; m.index.Len() > 0 && (*m.index)[0] == next; next++ {
   220→		ready = append(ready, m.items[next])
   221→		delete(m.items, next)
   222→		heap.Pop(m.index)
   223→	}
   224→	m.cacheMu.Lock()
   225→	m.cache = nil
   226→	m.cacheMu.Unlock()
   227→
   228→	return ready
   229→}
   230→
   231→// Len returns the length of the transaction map.
   232→func (m *SortedMap) Len() int {
   233→	return len(m.items)
   234→}
   235→
   236→func (m *SortedMap) flatten() types.Transactions {
   237→	m.cacheMu.Lock()
   238→	defer m.cacheMu.Unlock()
   239→	// If the sorting was not cached yet, create and cache it
   240→	if m.cache == nil {
   241→		m.cache = make(types.Transactions, 0, len(m.items))
   242→		for _, tx := range m.items {
   243→			m.cache = append(m.cache, tx)
   244→		}
   245→		sort.Sort(types.TxByNonce(m.cache))
   246→	}
   247→	return m.cache
   248→}
   249→
   250→// Flatten creates a nonce-sorted slice of transactions based on the loosely
   251→// sorted internal representation. The result of the sorting is cached in case
   252→// it's requested again before any modifications are made to the contents.
   253→func (m *SortedMap) Flatten() types.Transactions {
   254→	cache := m.flatten()
   255→	// Copy the cache to prevent accidental modification
   256→	txs := make(types.Transactions, len(cache))
   257→	copy(txs, cache)
   258→	return txs
   259→}
   260→
   261→// LastElement returns the last element of a flattened list, thus, the
   262→// transaction with the highest nonce
   263→func (m *SortedMap) LastElement() *types.Transaction {
   264→	cache := m.flatten()
   265→	return cache[len(cache)-1]
   266→}
   267→
   268→// list is a "list" of transactions belonging to an account, sorted by account
   269→// nonce. The same type can be used both for storing contiguous transactions for
   270→// the executable/pending queue; and for storing gapped transactions for the non-
   271→// executable/future queue, with minor behavioral changes.
   272→type list struct {
   273→	strict bool       // Whether nonces are strictly continuous or not
   274→	txs    *SortedMap // Heap indexed sorted hash map of the transactions
   275→
   276→	costcap   *uint256.Int // Price of the highest costing transaction (reset only if exceeds balance)
   277→	gascap    uint64       // Gas limit of the highest spending transaction (reset only if exceeds block limit)
   278→	totalcost *uint256.Int // Total cost of all transactions in the list
   279→}
   280→
   281→// newList creates a new transaction list for maintaining nonce-indexable fast,
   282→// gapped, sortable transaction lists.
   283→func newList(strict bool) *list {
   284→	return &list{
   285→		strict:    strict,
   286→		txs:       NewSortedMap(),
   287→		costcap:   new(uint256.Int),
   288→		totalcost: new(uint256.Int),
   289→	}
   290→}
   291→
   292→// Contains returns whether the  list contains a transaction
   293→// with the provided nonce.
   294→func (l *list) Contains(nonce uint64) bool {
   295→	return l.txs.Get(nonce) != nil
   296→}
   297→
   298→// Add tries to insert a new transaction into the list, returning whether the
   299→// transaction was accepted, and if yes, any previous transaction it replaced.
   300→//
   301→// If the new transaction is accepted into the list, the lists' cost and gas
   302→// thresholds are also potentially updated.
   303→func (l *list) Add(tx *types.Transaction, priceBump uint64) (bool, *types.Transaction) {
   304→	// If there's an older better transaction, abort
   305→	old := l.txs.Get(tx.Nonce())
   306→	if old != nil {
   307→		if old.GasFeeCapCmp(tx) >= 0 || old.GasTipCapCmp(tx) >= 0 {
   308→			return false, nil
   309→		}
   310→		// thresholdFeeCap = oldFC  * (100 + priceBump) / 100
   311→		a := big.NewInt(100 + int64(priceBump))
   312→		aFeeCap := new(big.Int).Mul(a, old.GasFeeCap())
   313→		aTip := a.Mul(a, old.GasTipCap())
   314→
   315→		// thresholdTip    = oldTip * (100 + priceBump) / 100
   316→		b := big.NewInt(100)
   317→		thresholdFeeCap := aFeeCap.Div(aFeeCap, b)
   318→		thresholdTip := aTip.Div(aTip, b)
   319→
   320→		// We have to ensure that both the new fee cap and tip are higher than the
   321→		// old ones as well as checking the percentage threshold to ensure that
   322→		// this is accurate for low (Wei-level) gas price replacements.
   323→		if tx.GasFeeCapIntCmp(thresholdFeeCap) < 0 || tx.GasTipCapIntCmp(thresholdTip) < 0 {
   324→			return false, nil
   325→		}
   326→	}
   327→	// Add new tx cost to totalcost
   328→	cost, overflow := uint256.FromBig(tx.Cost())
   329→	if overflow {
   330→		return false, nil
   331→	}
   332→	total, overflow := new(uint256.Int).AddOverflow(l.totalcost, cost)
   333→	if overflow {
   334→		return false, nil
   335→	}
   336→	l.totalcost = total
   337→
   338→	// Old is being replaced, subtract old cost
   339→	if old != nil {
   340→		l.subTotalCost([]*types.Transaction{old})
   341→	}
   342→
   343→	// Otherwise overwrite the old transaction with the current one
   344→	l.txs.Put(tx)
   345→	if l.costcap.Cmp(cost) < 0 {
   346→		l.costcap = cost
   347→	}
   348→	if gas := tx.Gas(); l.gascap < gas {
   349→		l.gascap = gas
   350→	}
   351→	return true, old
   352→}
   353→
   354→// Forward removes all transactions from the list with a nonce lower than the
   355→// provided threshold. Every removed transaction is returned for any post-removal
   356→// maintenance.
   357→func (l *list) Forward(threshold uint64) types.Transactions {
   358→	txs := l.txs.Forward(threshold)
   359→	l.subTotalCost(txs)
   360→	return txs
   361→}
   362→
   363→// Filter removes all transactions from the list with a cost or gas limit higher
   364→// than the provided thresholds. Every removed transaction is returned for any
   365→// post-removal maintenance. Strict-mode invalidated transactions are also
   366→// returned.
   367→//
   368→// This method uses the cached costcap and gascap to quickly decide if there's even
   369→// a point in calculating all the costs or if the balance covers all. If the threshold
   370→// is lower than the costgas cap, the caps will be reset to a new high after removing
   371→// the newly invalidated transactions.
   372→func (l *list) Filter(costLimit *uint256.Int, gasLimit uint64) (types.Transactions, types.Transactions) {
   373→	// If all transactions are below the threshold, short circuit
   374→	if l.costcap.Cmp(costLimit) <= 0 && l.gascap <= gasLimit {
   375→		return nil, nil
   376→	}
   377→	l.costcap = new(uint256.Int).Set(costLimit) // Lower the caps to the thresholds
   378→	l.gascap = gasLimit
   379→
   380→	// Filter out all the transactions above the account's funds
   381→	removed := l.txs.Filter(func(tx *types.Transaction) bool {
   382→		return tx.Gas() > gasLimit || tx.Cost().Cmp(costLimit.ToBig()) > 0
   383→	})
   384→
   385→	if len(removed) == 0 {
   386→		return nil, nil
   387→	}
   388→	var invalids types.Transactions
   389→	// If the list was strict, filter anything above the lowest nonce
   390→	if l.strict {
   391→		lowest := uint64(math.MaxUint64)
   392→		for _, tx := range removed {
   393→			if nonce := tx.Nonce(); lowest > nonce {
   394→				lowest = nonce
   395→			}
   396→		}
   397→		invalids = l.txs.filter(func(tx *types.Transaction) bool { return tx.Nonce() > lowest })
   398→	}
   399→	// Reset total cost
   400→	l.subTotalCost(removed)
   401→	l.subTotalCost(invalids)
   402→	l.txs.reheap()
   403→	return removed, invalids
   404→}
   405→
   406→// Cap places a hard limit on the number of items, returning all transactions
   407→// exceeding that limit.
   408→func (l *list) Cap(threshold int) types.Transactions {
   409→	txs := l.txs.Cap(threshold)
   410→	l.subTotalCost(txs)
   411→	return txs
   412→}
   413→
   414→// Remove deletes a transaction from the maintained list, returning whether the
   415→// transaction was found, and also returning any transaction invalidated due to
   416→// the deletion (strict mode only).
   417→func (l *list) Remove(tx *types.Transaction) (bool, types.Transactions) {
   418→	// Remove the transaction from the set
   419→	nonce := tx.Nonce()
   420→	if removed := l.txs.Remove(nonce); !removed {
   421→		return false, nil
   422→	}
   423→	l.subTotalCost([]*types.Transaction{tx})
   424→	// In strict mode, filter out non-executable transactions
   425→	if l.strict {
   426→		txs := l.txs.Filter(func(tx *types.Transaction) bool { return tx.Nonce() > nonce })
   427→		l.subTotalCost(txs)
   428→		return true, txs
   429→	}
   430→	return true, nil
   431→}
   432→
   433→// Ready retrieves a sequentially increasing list of transactions starting at the
   434→// provided nonce that is ready for processing. The returned transactions will be
   435→// removed from the list.
   436→//
   437→// Note, all transactions with nonces lower than start will also be returned to
   438→// prevent getting into an invalid state. This is not something that should ever
   439→// happen but better to be self correcting than failing!
   440→func (l *list) Ready(start uint64) types.Transactions {
   441→	txs := l.txs.Ready(start)
   442→	l.subTotalCost(txs)
   443→	return txs
   444→}
   445→
   446→// Len returns the length of the transaction list.
   447→func (l *list) Len() int {
   448→	return l.txs.Len()
   449→}
   450→
   451→// Empty returns whether the list of transactions is empty or not.
   452→func (l *list) Empty() bool {

   454→}
   455→
   456→// Flatten creates a nonce-sorted slice of transactions based on the loosely
   457→// sorted internal representation. The result of the sorting is cached in case
   458→// it's requested again before any modifications are made to the contents.
   459→func (l *list) Flatten() types.Transactions {
   460→	return l.txs.Flatten()
   461→}
   462→
   463→// LastElement returns the last element of a flattened list, thus, the
   464→// transaction with the highest nonce
   465→func (l *list) LastElement() *types.Transaction {
   466→	return l.txs.LastElement()
   467→}
   468→
   469→// subTotalCost subtracts the cost of the given transactions from the
   470→// total cost of all transactions.
   471→func (l *list) subTotalCost(txs []*types.Transaction) {
   472→	for _, tx := range txs {
   473→		_, underflow := l.totalcost.SubOverflow(l.totalcost, uint256.MustFromBig(tx.Cost()))
   474→		if underflow {
   475→			panic("totalcost underflow")
   476→		}
   477→	}
   478→}
   479→
   480→// priceHeap is a heap.Interface implementation over transactions for retrieving
   481→// price-sorted transactions to discard when the pool fills up. If baseFee is set
   482→// then the heap is sorted based on the effective tip based on the given base fee.
   483→// If baseFee is nil then the sorting is based on gasFeeCap.
   484→type priceHeap struct {
   485→	baseFee *uint256.Int // heap should always be re-sorted after baseFee is changed
   486→	list    []*types.Transaction
   487→}
   488→
   489→func (h *priceHeap) Len() int      { return len(h.list) }
   490→func (h *priceHeap) Swap(i, j int) { h.list[i], h.list[j] = h.list[j], h.list[i] }
   491→
   492→func (h *priceHeap) Less(i, j int) bool {
   493→	switch h.cmp(h.list[i], h.list[j]) {
   494→	case -1:
   495→		return true
   496→	case 1:
   497→		return false
   498→	default:
   499→		return h.list[i].Nonce() > h.list[j].Nonce()
   500→	}
   501→}
   502→
   503→func (h *priceHeap) cmp(a, b *types.Transaction) int {
   504→	if h.baseFee != nil {
   505→		// Compare effective tips if baseFee is specified
   506→		if c := a.EffectiveGasTipCmp(b, h.baseFee); c != 0 {
   507→			return c
   508→		}
   509→	}
   510→	// Compare fee caps if baseFee is not specified or effective tips are equal
   511→	if c := a.GasFeeCapCmp(b); c != 0 {
   512→		return c
   513→	}
   514→	// Compare tips if effective tips and fee caps are equal
   515→	return a.GasTipCapCmp(b)
   516→}
   517→
   518→func (h *priceHeap) Push(x interface{}) {
   519→	tx := x.(*types.Transaction)
   520→	h.list = append(h.list, tx)
   521→}
   522→
   523→func (h *priceHeap) Pop() interface{} {
   524→	old := h.list
   525→	n := len(old)
   526→	x := old[n-1]
   527→	old[n-1] = nil
   528→	h.list = old[0 : n-1]
   529→	return x
   530→}
   531→
   532→// pricedList is a price-sorted heap to allow operating on transactions pool
   533→// contents in a price-incrementing way. It's built upon the all transactions
   534→// in txpool but only interested in the remote part. It means only remote transactions
   535→// will be considered for tracking, sorting, eviction, etc.
   536→//
   537→// Two heaps are used for sorting: the urgent heap (based on effective tip in the next
   538→// block) and the floating heap (based on gasFeeCap). Always the bigger heap is chosen for
   539→// eviction. Transactions evicted from the urgent heap are first demoted into the floating heap.
   540→// In some cases (during a congestion, when blocks are full) the urgent heap can provide
   541→// better candidates for inclusion while in other cases (at the top of the baseFee peak)
   542→// the floating heap is better. When baseFee is decreasing they behave similarly.
   543→type pricedList struct {
   544→	// Number of stale price points to (re-heap trigger).
   545→	stales atomic.Int64
   546→
   547→	all              *lookup    // Pointer to the map of all transactions
   548→	urgent, floating priceHeap  // Heaps of prices of all the stored **remote** transactions
   549→	reheapMu         sync.Mutex // Mutex asserts that only one routine is reheaping the list
   550→}
   551→
   552→const (
   553→	// urgentRatio : floatingRatio is the capacity ratio of the two queues
   554→	urgentRatio   = 4
   555→	floatingRatio = 1
   556→)
   557→
   558→// newPricedList creates a new price-sorted transaction heap.
   559→func newPricedList(all *lookup) *pricedList {
   560→	return &pricedList{
   561→		all: all,
   562→	}
   563→}
   564→
   565→// Put inserts a new transaction into the heap.
   566→func (l *pricedList) Put(tx *types.Transaction) {
   567→	// Insert every new transaction to the urgent heap first; Discard will balance the heaps
   568→	heap.Push(&l.urgent, tx)
   569→}
   570→
   571→// Removed notifies the prices transaction list that an old transaction dropped
   572→// from the pool. The list will just keep a counter of stale objects and update
   573→// the heap if a large enough ratio of transactions go stale.
   574→func (l *pricedList) Removed(count int) {
   575→	// Bump the stale counter, but exit if still too low (< 25%)
   576→	stales := l.stales.Add(int64(count))
   577→	if int(stales) <= (len(l.urgent.list)+len(l.floating.list))/4 {
   578→		return
   579→	}
   580→	// Seems we've reached a critical number of stale transactions, reheap
   581→	l.Reheap()
   582→}
   583→
   584→// Underpriced checks whether a transaction is cheaper than (or as cheap as) the
   585→// lowest priced (remote) transaction currently being tracked.
   586→func (l *pricedList) Underpriced(tx *types.Transaction) bool {
   587→	// Note: with two queues, being underpriced is defined as being worse than the worst item
   588→	// in all non-empty queues if there is any. If both queues are empty then nothing is underpriced.
   589→	return (l.underpricedFor(&l.urgent, tx) || len(l.urgent.list) == 0) &&
   590→		(l.underpricedFor(&l.floating, tx) || len(l.floating.list) == 0) &&
   591→		(len(l.urgent.list) != 0 || len(l.floating.list) != 0)
   592→}
   593→
   594→// underpricedFor checks whether a transaction is cheaper than (or as cheap as) the
   595→// lowest priced (remote) transaction in the given heap.
   596→func (l *pricedList) underpricedFor(h *priceHeap, tx *types.Transaction) bool {
   597→	// Discard stale price points if found at the heap start
   598→	for len(h.list) > 0 {
   599→		head := h.list[0]
   600→		if l.all.Get(head.Hash()) == nil { // Removed or migrated
   601→			l.stales.Add(-1)
   602→			heap.Pop(h)
   603→			continue
   604→		}
   605→		break
   606→	}
   607→	// Check if the transaction is underpriced or not
   608→	if len(h.list) == 0 {
   609→		return false // There is no remote transaction at all.
   610→	}
   611→	// If the remote transaction is even cheaper than the
   612→	// cheapest one tracked locally, reject it.
   613→	return h.cmp(h.list[0], tx) >= 0
   614→}
   615→
   616→// Discard finds a number of most underpriced transactions, removes them from the
   617→// priced list and returns them for further removal from the entire pool.
   618→// If noPending is set to true, we will only consider the floating list
   619→func (l *pricedList) Discard(slots int) (types.Transactions, bool) {
   620→	drop := make(types.Transactions, 0, slots) // Remote underpriced transactions to drop
   621→	for slots > 0 {
   622→		if len(l.urgent.list)*floatingRatio > len(l.floating.list)*urgentRatio {
   623→			// Discard stale transactions if found during cleanup
   624→			tx := heap.Pop(&l.urgent).(*types.Transaction)
   625→			if l.all.Get(tx.Hash()) == nil { // Removed or migrated
   626→				l.stales.Add(-1)
   627→				continue
   628→			}
   629→			// Non stale transaction found, move to floating heap
   630→			heap.Push(&l.floating, tx)
   631→		} else {
   632→			if len(l.floating.list) == 0 {
   633→				// Stop if both heaps are empty
   634→				break
   635→			}
   636→			// Discard stale transactions if found during cleanup
   637→			tx := heap.Pop(&l.floating).(*types.Transaction)
   638→			if l.all.Get(tx.Hash()) == nil { // Removed or migrated
   639→				l.stales.Add(-1)
   640→				continue
   641→			}
   642→			// Non stale transaction found, discard it
   643→			drop = append(drop, tx)
   644→			slots -= numSlots(tx)
   645→		}
   646→	}
   647→	// If we still can't make enough room for the new transaction
   648→	if slots > 0 {
   649→		for _, tx := range drop {
   650→			heap.Push(&l.urgent, tx)
   651→		}
   652→		return nil, false
   653→	}
   654→	return drop, true
   655→}
