   744→// Finalise finalises the state by removing the destructed objects and clears
   745→// the journal as well as the refunds. Finalise, however, will not push any updates
   746→// into the tries just yet. Only IntermediateRoot or Commit will do that.
   747→func (s *StateDB) Finalise(deleteEmptyObjects bool) {
   748→	addressesToPrefetch := make([]common.Address, 0, len(s.journal.dirties))
   749→	for addr := range s.journal.dirties {
   750→		obj, exist := s.stateObjects[addr]
   751→		if !exist {
   752→			// ripeMD is 'touched' at block 1714175, in tx 0x1237f737031e40bcde4a8b7e717b2d15e3ecadfe49bb1bbc71ee9deb09c6fcf2
   753→			// That tx goes out of gas, and although the notion of 'touched' does not exist there, the
   754→			// touch-event will still be recorded in the journal. Since ripeMD is a special snowflake,
   755→			// it will persist in the journal even though the journal is reverted. In this special circumstance,
   756→			// it may exist in `s.journal.dirties` but not in `s.stateObjects`.
   757→			// Thus, we can safely ignore it here
   758→			continue
   759→		}
   760→		if obj.selfDestructed || (deleteEmptyObjects && obj.empty()) {
   761→			delete(s.stateObjects, obj.address)
   762→			s.markDelete(addr)
   763→			// We need to maintain account deletions explicitly (will remain
   764→			// set indefinitely). Note only the first occurred self-destruct
   765→			// event is tracked.
   766→			if _, ok := s.stateObjectsDestruct[obj.address]; !ok {
   767→				s.stateObjectsDestruct[obj.address] = obj
   768→			}
   769→		} else {
   770→			obj.finalise()
   771→			s.markUpdate(addr)
   772→		}
   773→		// At this point, also ship the address off to the precacher. The precacher
   774→		// will start loading tries, and when the change is eventually committed,
   775→		// the commit-phase will be a lot faster
   776→		addressesToPrefetch = append(addressesToPrefetch, addr) // Copy needed for closure
   777→	}
   778→	if s.prefetcher != nil && len(addressesToPrefetch) > 0 {
   779→		if err := s.prefetcher.prefetch(common.Hash{}, s.originalRoot, common.Address{}, addressesToPrefetch, nil, false); err != nil {
   780→			log.Error("Failed to prefetch addresses", "addresses", len(addressesToPrefetch), "err", err)
   781→		}
   782→	}
   783→	// Invalidate journal because reverting across transactions is not allowed.
   784→	s.clearJournalAndRefund()
   785→}

   787→// IntermediateRoot computes the current root hash of the state trie.
   788→// It is called in between transactions to get the root hash that
   789→// goes into transaction receipts.
   790→func (s *StateDB) IntermediateRoot(deleteEmptyObjects bool) common.Hash {
   791→	// Finalise all the dirty storage states and write them into the tries
   792→	s.Finalise(deleteEmptyObjects)
   793→
   794→	// Initialize the trie if it's not constructed yet. If the prefetch
   795→	// is enabled, the trie constructed below will be replaced by the
   796→	// prefetched one.
   797→	//
   798→	// This operation must be done before state object storage hashing,
   799→	// as it assumes the main trie is already loaded.
   800→	if s.trie == nil {
   801→		tr, err := s.db.OpenTrie(s.originalRoot)
   802→		if err != nil {
   803→			s.setError(err)
   804→			return common.Hash{}
   805→		}
   806→		s.trie = tr
   807→	}
   808→	// If there was a trie prefetcher operating, terminate it async so that the
   809→	// individual storage tries can be updated as soon as the disk load finishes.
   810→	if s.prefetcher != nil {
   811→		s.prefetcher.terminate(true)
   812→		defer func() {
   813→			s.prefetcher.report()
   814→			s.prefetcher = nil // Pre-byzantium, unset any used up prefetcher
   815→		}()
   816→	}
   817→	// Process all storage updates concurrently. The state object update root
   818→	// method will internally call a blocking trie fetch from the prefetcher,
   819→	// so there's no need to explicitly wait for the prefetchers to finish.
   820→	var (
   821→		start   = time.Now()
   822→		workers errgroup.Group
   823→	)
   824→	if s.db.TrieDB().IsVerkle() {
   825→		// Whilst MPT storage tries are independent, Verkle has one single trie
   826→		// for all the accounts and all the storage slots merged together. The
   827→		// former can thus be simply parallelized, but updating the latter will
   828→		// need concurrency support within the trie itself. That's a TODO for a
   829→		// later time.
   830→		workers.SetLimit(1)
   831→	}
   832→	for addr, op := range s.mutations {
   833→		if op.applied || op.isDelete() {
   834→			continue
   835→		}
   836→		obj := s.stateObjects[addr] // closure for the task runner below
   837→		workers.Go(func() error {
   838→			if s.db.TrieDB().IsVerkle() {
   839→				obj.updateTrie()
   840→			} else {
   841→				obj.updateRoot()
   842→
   843→				// If witness building is enabled and the state object has a trie,
   844→				// gather the witnesses for its specific storage trie
   845→				if s.witness != nil && obj.trie != nil {
   846→					s.witness.AddState(obj.trie.Witness())
   847→				}
   848→			}
   849→			return nil
   850→		})
   851→	}
   852→	// If witness building is enabled, gather all the read-only accesses.
   853→	// Skip witness collection in Verkle mode, they will be gathered
   854→	// together at the end.
   855→	if s.witness != nil && !s.db.TrieDB().IsVerkle() {
   856→		// Pull in anything that has been accessed before destruction
   857→		for _, obj := range s.stateObjectsDestruct {
   858→			// Skip any objects that haven't touched their storage
   859→			if len(obj.originStorage) == 0 {
   860→				continue
   861→			}
   862→			if trie := obj.getPrefetchedTrie(); trie != nil {
   863→				witness := trie.Witness()
   864→				s.witness.AddState(witness)
   865→				if s.witnessStats != nil {
   866→					s.witnessStats.Add(witness, obj.addrHash)
   867→				}
   868→			} else if obj.trie != nil {
   869→				witness := obj.trie.Witness()
   870→				s.witness.AddState(witness)
   871→				if s.witnessStats != nil {
   872→					s.witnessStats.Add(witness, obj.addrHash)
   873→				}
   874→			}
   875→		}
   876→		// Pull in only-read and non-destructed trie witnesses
   877→		for _, obj := range s.stateObjects {
   878→			// Skip any objects that have been updated
   879→			if _, ok := s.mutations[obj.address]; ok {
   880→				continue
   881→			}
   882→			// Skip any objects that haven't touched their storage
   883→			if len(obj.originStorage) == 0 {
   884→				continue
   885→			}
   886→			if trie := obj.getPrefetchedTrie(); trie != nil {
   887→				witness := trie.Witness()
   888→				s.witness.AddState(witness)
   889→				if s.witnessStats != nil {
   890→					s.witnessStats.Add(witness, obj.addrHash)
   891→				}
   892→			} else if obj.trie != nil {
   893→				witness := obj.trie.Witness()
   894→				s.witness.AddState(witness)
   895→				if s.witnessStats != nil {
   896→					s.witnessStats.Add(witness, obj.addrHash)
   897→				}
   898→			}
   899→		}
   900→	}
   901→	workers.Wait()
   902→	s.StorageUpdates += time.Since(start)
   903→
   904→	// Now we're about to start to write changes to the trie. The trie is so far
   905→	// _untouched_. We can check with the prefetcher, if it can give us a trie
   906→	// which has the same root, but also has some content loaded into it.
   907→	//
   908→	// Don't check prefetcher if verkle trie has been used. In the context of verkle,
   909→	// only a single trie is used for state hashing. Replacing a non-nil verkle tree
   910→	// here could result in losing uncommitted changes from storage.
   911→	start = time.Now()
   912→	if s.prefetcher != nil {
   913→		if trie := s.prefetcher.trie(common.Hash{}, s.originalRoot); trie == nil {
   914→			log.Error("Failed to retrieve account pre-fetcher trie")
   915→		} else {
   916→			s.trie = trie
   917→		}
   918→	}
   919→	// Perform updates before deletions.  This prevents resolution of unnecessary trie nodes
   920→	// in circumstances similar to the following:
   921→	//
   922→	// Consider nodes `A` and `B` who share the same full node parent `P` and have no other siblings.
   923→	// During the execution of a block:
   924→	// - `A` self-destructs,
   925→	// - `C` is created, and also shares the parent `P`.
   926→	// If the self-destruct is handled first, then `P` would be left with only one child, thus collapsed
   927→	// into a shortnode. This requires `B` to be resolved from disk.
   928→	// Whereas if the created node is handled first, then the collapse is avoided, and `B` is not resolved.
   929→	var (
   930→		usedAddrs    []common.Address
   931→		deletedAddrs []common.Address
   932→	)
   933→	for addr, op := range s.mutations {
   934→		if op.applied {
   935→			continue
   936→		}
   937→		op.applied = true
   938→
   939→		if op.isDelete() {
   940→			deletedAddrs = append(deletedAddrs, addr)
   941→		} else {
   942→			s.updateStateObject(s.stateObjects[addr])
   943→			s.AccountUpdated += 1
   944→		}
   945→		usedAddrs = append(usedAddrs, addr) // Copy needed for closure
   946→	}
   947→	for _, deletedAddr := range deletedAddrs {
   948→		s.deleteStateObject(deletedAddr)
   949→		s.AccountDeleted += 1
   950→	}
   951→	s.AccountUpdates += time.Since(start)
   952→
   953→	if s.prefetcher != nil {
   954→		s.prefetcher.used(common.Hash{}, s.originalRoot, usedAddrs, nil)
   955→	}
   956→	// Track the amount of time wasted on hashing the account trie
   957→	defer func(start time.Time) { s.AccountHashes += time.Since(start) }(time.Now())
   958→
   959→	hash := s.trie.Hash()
   960→
   961→	// If witness building is enabled, gather the account trie witness
   962→	if s.witness != nil {
   963→		witness := s.trie.Witness()
   964→		s.witness.AddState(witness)
   965→		if s.witnessStats != nil {
   966→			s.witnessStats.Add(witness, common.Hash{})
   967→		}
   968→	}
   969→	return hash
   970→}

   985→// fastDeleteStorage is the function that efficiently deletes the storage trie
   986→// of a specific account. It leverages the associated state snapshot for fast
   987→// storage iteration and constructs trie node deletion markers by creating
   988→// stack trie with iterated slots.
   989→func (s *StateDB) fastDeleteStorage(snaps *snapshot.Tree, addrHash common.Hash, root common.Hash) (map[common.Hash][]byte, map[common.Hash][]byte, *trienode.NodeSet, error) {
   990→	iter, err := snaps.StorageIterator(s.originalRoot, addrHash, common.Hash{})
   991→	if err != nil {
   992→		return nil, nil, nil, err
   993→	}
   994→	defer iter.Release()
   995→
   996→	var (
   997→		nodes          = trienode.NewNodeSet(addrHash) // the set for trie node mutations (value is nil)
   998→		storages       = make(map[common.Hash][]byte)  // the set for storage mutations (value is nil)
   999→		storageOrigins = make(map[common.Hash][]byte)  // the set for tracking the original value of slot
  1000→	)
  1001→	stack := trie.NewStackTrie(func(path []byte, hash common.Hash, blob []byte) {
  1002→		nodes.AddNode(path, trienode.NewDeletedWithPrev(blob))
  1003→	})
  1004→	for iter.Next() {
  1005→		slot := common.CopyBytes(iter.Slot())
  1006→		if err := iter.Error(); err != nil { // error might occur after Slot function
  1007→			return nil, nil, nil, err
  1008→		}
  1009→		key := iter.Hash()
  1010→		storages[key] = nil
  1011→		storageOrigins[key] = slot
  1012→
  1013→		if err := stack.Update(key.Bytes(), slot); err != nil {
  1014→			return nil, nil, nil, err
  1015→		}
  1016→	}
  1017→	if err := iter.Error(); err != nil { // error might occur during iteration
  1018→		return nil, nil, nil, err
  1019→	}
  1020→	if stack.Hash() != root {
  1021→		return nil, nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("snapshot is not matched, exp %x, got %x", root, stack.Hash())
  1022→	}
  1023→	return storages, storageOrigins, nodes, nil
  1024→}

  1026→// slowDeleteStorage serves as a less-efficient alternative to "fastDeleteStorage,"
  1027→// employed when the associated state snapshot is not available. It iterates the
  1028→// storage slots along with all internal trie nodes via trie directly.
  1029→func (s *StateDB) slowDeleteStorage(addr common.Address, addrHash common.Hash, root common.Hash) (map[common.Hash][]byte, map[common.Hash][]byte, *trienode.NodeSet, error) {
  1030→	tr, err := s.db.OpenStorageTrie(s.originalRoot, addr, root, s.trie)
  1031→	if err != nil {
  1032→		return nil, nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to open storage trie, err: %w", err)
  1033→	}
  1034→	it, err := tr.NodeIterator(nil)
  1035→	if err != nil {
  1036→		return nil, nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to open storage iterator, err: %w", err)
  1037→	}
  1038→	var (
  1039→		nodes          = trienode.NewNodeSet(addrHash) // the set for trie node mutations (value is nil)
  1040→		storages       = make(map[common.Hash][]byte)  // the set for storage mutations (value is nil)
  1041→		storageOrigins = make(map[common.Hash][]byte)  // the set for tracking the original value of slot
  1042→	)
  1043→	for it.Next(true) {
  1044→		if it.Leaf() {
  1045→			key := common.BytesToHash(it.LeafKey())
  1046→			storages[key] = nil
  1047→			storageOrigins[key] = common.CopyBytes(it.LeafBlob())
  1048→			continue
  1049→		}
  1050→		if it.Hash() == (common.Hash{}) {
  1051→			continue
  1052→		}
  1053→		nodes.AddNode(it.Path(), trienode.NewDeletedWithPrev(it.NodeBlob()))
  1054→	}
  1055→	if err := it.Error(); err != nil {
  1056→		return nil, nil, nil, err
  1057→	}
  1058→	return storages, storageOrigins, nodes, nil
  1059→}
  1060→
  1061→// deleteStorage is designed to delete the storage trie of a designated account.
  1062→// The function will make an attempt to utilize an efficient strategy if the
  1063→// associated state snapshot is reachable; otherwise, it will resort to a less
  1064→// efficient approach.
  1065→func (s *StateDB) deleteStorage(addr common.Address, addrHash common.Hash, root common.Hash) (map[common.Hash][]byte, map[common.Hash][]byte, *trienode.NodeSet, error) {
  1066→	var (
  1067→		err            error
  1068→		nodes          *trienode.NodeSet      // the set for trie node mutations (value is nil)
  1069→		storages       map[common.Hash][]byte // the set for storage mutations (value is nil)
  1070→		storageOrigins map[common.Hash][]byte // the set for tracking the original value of slot
  1071→	)
  1072→	// The fast approach can be failed if the snapshot is not fully
  1073→	// generated, or it's internally corrupted. Fallback to the slow
  1074→	// one just in case.
  1075→	snaps := s.db.Snapshot()
  1076→	if snaps != nil {
  1077→		storages, storageOrigins, nodes, err = s.fastDeleteStorage(snaps, addrHash, root)
  1078→	}
  1079→	if snaps == nil || err != nil {
  1080→		storages, storageOrigins, nodes, err = s.slowDeleteStorage(addr, addrHash, root)
  1081→	}
  1082→	if err != nil {
  1083→		return nil, nil, nil, err
  1084→	}
  1085→	return storages, storageOrigins, nodes, nil
  1086→}
  1087→
  1088→// handleDestruction processes all destruction markers and deletes the account
  1089→// and associated storage slots if necessary. There are four potential scenarios
  1090→// as following:
  1091→//
  1092→//	(a) the account was not existent and be marked as destructed
  1093→//	(b) the account was not existent and be marked as destructed,
  1094→//	    however, it's resurrected later in the same block.
  1095→//	(c) the account was existent and be marked as destructed
  1096→//	(d) the account was existent and be marked as destructed,
  1097→//	    however it's resurrected later in the same block.
  1098→//
  1099→// In case (a), nothing needs be deleted, nil to nil transition can be ignored.
  1100→// In case (b), nothing needs be deleted, nil is used as the original value for
  1101→// newly created account and storages
  1102→// In case (c), **original** account along with its storages should be deleted,
  1103→// with their values be tracked as original value.
  1104→// In case (d), **original** account along with its storages should be deleted,
  1105→// with their values be tracked as original value.
  1106→func (s *StateDB) handleDestruction(noStorageWiping bool) (map[common.Hash]*accountDelete, []*trienode.NodeSet, error) {
  1107→	var (
  1108→		nodes   []*trienode.NodeSet
  1109→		deletes = make(map[common.Hash]*accountDelete)
  1110→	)
  1111→	for addr, prevObj := range s.stateObjectsDestruct {
  1112→		prev := prevObj.origin
  1113→
  1114→		// The account was non-existent, and it's marked as destructed in the scope
  1115→		// of block. It can be either case (a) or (b) and will be interpreted as
  1116→		// null->null state transition.
  1117→		// - for (a), skip it without doing anything
  1118→		// - for (b), the resurrected account with nil as original will be handled afterwards
  1119→		if prev == nil {
  1120→			continue
  1121→		}
  1122→		// The account was existent, it can be either case (c) or (d).
  1123→		addrHash := crypto.Keccak256Hash(addr.Bytes())
  1124→		op := &accountDelete{
  1125→			address: addr,
  1126→			origin:  types.SlimAccountRLP(*prev),
  1127→		}
  1128→		deletes[addrHash] = op
  1129→
  1130→		// Short circuit if the origin storage was empty.
  1131→		if prev.Root == types.EmptyRootHash || s.db.TrieDB().IsVerkle() {
  1132→			continue
  1133→		}
  1134→		if noStorageWiping {
  1135→			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("unexpected storage wiping, %x", addr)
  1136→		}
  1137→		// Remove storage slots belonging to the account.
  1138→		storages, storagesOrigin, set, err := s.deleteStorage(addr, addrHash, prev.Root)
  1139→		if err != nil {
  1140→			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to delete storage, err: %w", err)
  1141→		}
  1142→		op.storages = storages
  1143→		op.storagesOrigin = storagesOrigin
  1144→
  1145→		// Aggregate the associated trie node changes.
  1146→		nodes = append(nodes, set)
  1147→	}
  1148→	return deletes, nodes, nil
  1149→}

  1156→// commit gathers the state mutations accumulated along with the associated
  1157→// trie changes, resetting all internal flags with the new state as the base.
  1158→func (s *StateDB) commit(deleteEmptyObjects bool, noStorageWiping bool, blockNumber uint64) (*stateUpdate, error) {
  1159→	// Short circuit in case any database failure occurred earlier.
  1160→	if s.dbErr != nil {
  1161→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("commit aborted due to earlier error: %v", s.dbErr)
  1162→	}
  1163→	// Finalize any pending changes and merge everything into the tries
  1164→	s.IntermediateRoot(deleteEmptyObjects)
  1165→
  1166→	// Short circuit if any error occurs within the IntermediateRoot.
  1167→	if s.dbErr != nil {
  1168→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("commit aborted due to database error: %v", s.dbErr)
  1169→	}
  1170→	// Commit objects to the trie, measuring the elapsed time
  1171→	var (
  1172→		accountTrieNodesUpdated int
  1173→		accountTrieNodesDeleted int
  1174→		storageTrieNodesUpdated int
  1175→		storageTrieNodesDeleted int
  1176→
  1177→		lock    sync.Mutex                                               // protect two maps below
  1178→		nodes   = trienode.NewMergedNodeSet()                            // aggregated trie nodes
  1179→		updates = make(map[common.Hash]*accountUpdate, len(s.mutations)) // aggregated account updates
  1180→
  1181→		// merge aggregates the dirty trie nodes into the global set.
  1182→		//
  1183→		// Given that some accounts may be destroyed and then recreated within
  1184→		// the same block, it's possible that a node set with the same owner
  1185→		// may already exist. In such cases, these two sets are combined, with
  1186→		// the later one overwriting the previous one if any nodes are modified
  1187→		// or deleted in both sets.
  1188→		//
  1189→		// merge run concurrently across  all the state objects and account trie.
  1190→		merge = func(set *trienode.NodeSet) error {
  1191→			if set == nil {
  1192→				return nil
  1193→			}
  1194→			lock.Lock()
  1195→			defer lock.Unlock()
  1196→
  1197→			updates, deletes := set.Size()
  1198→			if set.Owner == (common.Hash{}) {
  1199→				accountTrieNodesUpdated += updates
  1200→				accountTrieNodesDeleted += deletes
  1201→			} else {
  1202→				storageTrieNodesUpdated += updates
  1203→				storageTrieNodesDeleted += deletes
  1204→			}
  1205→			return nodes.Merge(set)
  1206→		}
  1207→	)
  1208→	// Given that some accounts could be destroyed and then recreated within
  1209→	// the same block, account deletions must be processed first. This ensures
  1210→	// that the storage trie nodes deleted during destruction and recreated
  1211→	// during subsequent resurrection can be combined correctly.
  1212→	deletes, delNodes, err := s.handleDestruction(noStorageWiping)
  1213→	if err != nil {
  1214→		return nil, err
  1215→	}
  1216→	for _, set := range delNodes {
  1217→		if err := merge(set); err != nil {
  1218→			return nil, err
  1219→		}
  1220→	}
  1221→	// Handle all state updates afterwards, concurrently to one another to shave
  1222→	// off some milliseconds from the commit operation. Also accumulate the code
  1223→	// writes to run in parallel with the computations.
  1224→	var (
  1225→		start   = time.Now()
  1226→		root    common.Hash
  1227→		workers errgroup.Group
  1228→	)
  1229→	// Schedule the account trie first since that will be the biggest, so give
  1230→	// it the most time to crunch.
  1231→	//
  1232→	// TODO(karalabe): This account trie commit is *very* heavy. 5-6ms at chain
  1233→	// heads, which seems excessive given that it doesn't do hashing, it just
  1234→	// shuffles some data. For comparison, the *hashing* at chain head is 2-3ms.
  1235→	// We need to investigate what's happening as it seems something's wonky.
  1236→	// Obviously it's not an end of the world issue, just something the original
  1237→	// code didn't anticipate for.
  1238→	workers.Go(func() error {
  1239→		// Write the account trie changes, measuring the amount of wasted time
  1240→		newroot, set := s.trie.Commit(true)
  1241→		root = newroot
  1242→
  1243→		if err := merge(set); err != nil {
  1244→			return err
  1245→		}
  1246→		s.AccountCommits = time.Since(start)
  1247→		return nil
  1248→	})
  1249→	// Schedule each of the storage tries that need to be updated, so they can
  1250→	// run concurrently to one another.
  1251→	//
  1252→	// TODO(karalabe): Experimentally, the account commit takes approximately the
  1253→	// same time as all the storage commits combined, so we could maybe only have
  1254→	// 2 threads in total. But that kind of depends on the account commit being
  1255→	// more expensive than it should be, so let's fix that and revisit this todo.
  1256→	for addr, op := range s.mutations {
  1257→		if op.isDelete() {
  1258→			continue
  1259→		}
  1260→		// Write any contract code associated with the state object
  1261→		obj := s.stateObjects[addr]
  1262→		if obj == nil {
  1263→			return nil, errors.New("missing state object")
  1264→		}
  1265→		// Run the storage updates concurrently to one another
  1266→		workers.Go(func() error {
  1267→			// Write any storage changes in the state object to its storage trie
  1268→			update, set, err := obj.commit()
  1269→			if err != nil {
  1270→				return err
  1271→			}
  1272→			if err := merge(set); err != nil {
  1273→				return err
  1274→			}
  1275→			lock.Lock()
  1276→			updates[obj.addrHash] = update
  1277→			s.StorageCommits = time.Since(start) // overwrite with the longest storage commit runtime
  1278→			lock.Unlock()
  1279→			return nil
  1280→		})
  1281→	}
  1282→	// Wait for everything to finish and update the metrics
  1283→	if err := workers.Wait(); err != nil {
  1284→		return nil, err
  1285→	}
  1286→	accountReadMeters.Mark(int64(s.AccountLoaded))
  1287→	storageReadMeters.Mark(int64(s.StorageLoaded))
  1288→	accountUpdatedMeter.Mark(int64(s.AccountUpdated))
  1289→	storageUpdatedMeter.Mark(s.StorageUpdated.Load())
  1290→	accountDeletedMeter.Mark(int64(s.AccountDeleted))
  1291→	storageDeletedMeter.Mark(s.StorageDeleted.Load())
  1292→	accountTrieUpdatedMeter.Mark(int64(accountTrieNodesUpdated))
  1293→	accountTrieDeletedMeter.Mark(int64(accountTrieNodesDeleted))
  1294→	storageTriesUpdatedMeter.Mark(int64(storageTrieNodesUpdated))
  1295→	storageTriesDeletedMeter.Mark(int64(storageTrieNodesDeleted))
  1296→
  1297→	// Clear the metric markers
  1298→	s.AccountLoaded, s.AccountUpdated, s.AccountDeleted = 0, 0, 0
  1299→	s.StorageLoaded = 0
  1300→	s.StorageUpdated.Store(0)
  1301→	s.StorageDeleted.Store(0)
  1302→
  1303→	// Clear all internal flags and update state root at the end.
  1304→	s.mutations = make(map[common.Address]*mutation)
  1305→	s.stateObjectsDestruct = make(map[common.Address]*stateObject)
  1306→
  1307→	origin := s.originalRoot
  1308→	s.originalRoot = root
  1309→
  1310→	return newStateUpdate(noStorageWiping, origin, root, blockNumber, deletes, updates, nodes), nil
  1311→}

  1313→// commitAndFlush is a wrapper of commit which also commits the state mutations
  1314→// to the configured data stores.
  1315→func (s *StateDB) commitAndFlush(block uint64, deleteEmptyObjects bool, noStorageWiping bool) (*stateUpdate, error) {
  1316→	ret, err := s.commit(deleteEmptyObjects, noStorageWiping, block)
  1317→	if err != nil {
  1318→		return nil, err
  1319→	}
  1320→	// Commit dirty contract code if any exists
  1321→	if db := s.db.TrieDB().Disk(); db != nil && len(ret.codes) > 0 {
  1322→		batch := db.NewBatch()
  1323→		for _, code := range ret.codes {
  1324→			rawdb.WriteCode(batch, code.hash, code.blob)
  1325→		}
  1326→		if err := batch.Write(); err != nil {
  1327→			return nil, err
  1328→		}
  1329→	}
  1330→	if !ret.empty() {
  1331→		// If snapshotting is enabled, update the snapshot tree with this new version
  1332→		if snap := s.db.Snapshot(); snap != nil && snap.Snapshot(ret.originRoot) != nil {
  1333→			start := time.Now()
  1334→			if err := snap.Update(ret.root, ret.originRoot, ret.accounts, ret.storages); err != nil {
  1335→				log.Warn("Failed to update snapshot tree", "from", ret.originRoot, "to", ret.root, "err", err)
  1336→			}
  1337→			// Keep 128 diff layers in the memory, persistent layer is 129th.
  1338→			// - head layer is paired with HEAD state
  1339→			// - head-1 layer is paired with HEAD-1 state
  1340→			// - head-127 layer(bottom-most diff layer) is paired with HEAD-127 state
  1341→			if err := snap.Cap(ret.root, TriesInMemory); err != nil {
  1342→				log.Warn("Failed to cap snapshot tree", "root", ret.root, "layers", TriesInMemory, "err", err)
  1343→			}
  1344→			s.SnapshotCommits += time.Since(start)
  1345→		}
  1346→		// If trie database is enabled, commit the state update as a new layer
  1347→		if db := s.db.TrieDB(); db != nil {
  1348→			start := time.Now()
  1349→			if err := db.Update(ret.root, ret.originRoot, block, ret.nodes, ret.stateSet()); err != nil {
  1350→				return nil, err
  1351→			}
  1352→			s.TrieDBCommits += time.Since(start)
  1353→		}
  1354→	}
  1355→	s.reader, _ = s.db.Reader(s.originalRoot)
  1356→	return ret, err
  1357→}

  1359→// Commit writes the state mutations into the configured data stores.
  1360→//
  1361→// Once the state is committed, tries cached in stateDB (including account
  1362→// trie, storage tries) will no longer be functional. A new state instance
  1363→// must be created with new root and updated database for accessing post-
  1364→// commit states.
  1365→//
  1366→// The associated block number of the state transition is also provided
  1367→// for more chain context.
  1368→//
  1369→// noStorageWiping is a flag indicating whether storage wiping is permitted.
  1370→// Since self-destruction was deprecated with the Cancun fork and there are
  1371→// no empty accounts left that could be deleted by EIP-158, storage wiping
  1372→// should not occur.
  1373→func (s *StateDB) Commit(block uint64, deleteEmptyObjects bool, noStorageWiping bool) (common.Hash, error) {
  1374→	ret, err := s.commitAndFlush(block, deleteEmptyObjects, noStorageWiping)
  1375→	if err != nil {
  1376→		return common.Hash{}, err
  1377→	}
  1378→	return ret.root, nil
  1379→}

  1381→// CommitWithUpdate writes the state mutations and returns both the root hash and the state update.
  1382→// This is useful for tracking state changes at the blockchain level.
  1383→func (s *StateDB) CommitWithUpdate(block uint64, deleteEmptyObjects bool, noStorageWiping bool) (common.Hash, *stateUpdate, error) {
  1384→	ret, err := s.commitAndFlush(block, deleteEmptyObjects, noStorageWiping)
  1385→	if err != nil {
  1386→		return common.Hash{}, nil, err
  1387→	}
  1388→	return ret.root, ret, nil
  1389→}

  1391→// Prepare handles the preparatory steps for executing a state transition with.
  1392→// This method must be invoked before state transition.
  1393→//
  1394→// Berlin fork:
  1395→// - Add sender to access list (2929)
  1396→// - Add destination to access list (2929)
  1397→// - Add precompiles to access list (2929)
  1398→// - Add the contents of the optional tx access list (2930)
  1399→//
  1400→// Potential EIPs:
  1401→// - Reset access list (Berlin)
  1402→// - Add coinbase to access list (EIP-3651)
  1403→// - Reset transient storage (EIP-1153)
  1404→func (s *StateDB) Prepare(rules params.Rules, sender, coinbase common.Address, dst *common.Address, precompiles []common.Address, list types.AccessList) {
  1405→	if rules.IsEIP2929 && rules.IsEIP4762 {
  1406→		panic("eip2929 and eip4762 are both activated")
  1407→	}
  1408→	if rules.IsEIP2929 {
  1409→		// Clear out any leftover from previous executions
  1410→		al := newAccessList()
  1411→		s.accessList = al
  1412→
  1413→		al.AddAddress(sender)
  1414→		if dst != nil {
  1415→			al.AddAddress(*dst)
  1416→			// If it's a create-tx, the destination will be added inside evm.create
  1417→		}
  1418→		for _, addr := range precompiles {
  1419→			al.AddAddress(addr)
  1420→		}
  1421→		for _, el := range list {
  1422→			al.AddAddress(el.Address)
  1423→			for _, key := range el.StorageKeys {
  1424→				al.AddSlot(el.Address, key)
  1425→			}
  1426→		}
  1427→		if rules.IsShanghai { // EIP-3651: warm coinbase
  1428→			al.AddAddress(coinbase)
  1429→		}
  1430→	}
  1431→	// Reset transient storage at the beginning of transaction execution
  1432→	s.transientStorage = newTransientStorage()
  1433→}

  1436→func (s *StateDB) AddAddressToAccessList(addr common.Address) {
  1437→	if s.accessList.AddAddress(addr) {

  1442→// AddSlotToAccessList adds the given (address, slot)-tuple to the access list
  1443→func (s *StateDB) AddSlotToAccessList(addr common.Address, slot common.Hash) {
  1444→	addrMod, slotMod := s.accessList.AddSlot(addr, slot)
  1445→	if addrMod {
  1446→		// In practice, this should not happen, since there is no way to enter the
  1447→		// scope of 'address' without having the 'address' become already added
  1448→		// to the access list (via call-variant, create, etc).
  1449→		// Better safe than sorry, though
  1450→		s.journal.accessListAddAccount(addr)
  1451→	}
  1452→	if slotMod {
  1453→		s.journal.accessListAddSlot(addr, slot)
  1454→	}
  1455→}

    28→// transientStorage is a representation of EIP-1153 "Transient Storage".
    29→type transientStorage map[common.Address]Storage
    30→
    31→// newTransientStorage creates a new instance of a transientStorage.
    32→func newTransientStorage() transientStorage {
    33→	return make(transientStorage)
    34→}
    35→
    36→// Set sets the transient-storage `value` for `key` at the given `addr`.
    37→func (t transientStorage) Set(addr common.Address, key, value common.Hash) {
    38→	if value == (common.Hash{}) { // this is a 'delete'
    39→		if _, ok := t[addr]; ok {
    40→			delete(t[addr], key)
    41→			if len(t[addr]) == 0 {
    42→				delete(t, addr)
    43→			}
    44→		}
    45→	} else {
    46→		if _, ok := t[addr]; !ok {
    47→			t[addr] = make(Storage)
    48→		}
    49→		t[addr][key] = value
    50→	}
    51→}
    52→
    53→// Get gets the transient storage for `key` at the given `addr`.
    54→func (t transientStorage) Get(addr common.Address, key common.Hash) common.Hash {
    55→	val, ok := t[addr]
    56→	if !ok {
    57→		return common.Hash{}
    58→	}
    59→	return val[key]
    60→}
    61→
    62→// Copy does a deep copy of the transientStorage
    63→func (t transientStorage) Copy() transientStorage {
    64→	storage := make(transientStorage)
    65→	for key, value := range t {
    66→		storage[key] = value.Copy()
    67→	}
    68→	return storage
    69→}

    71→// PrettyPrint prints the contents of the access list in a human-readable form
    72→func (t transientStorage) PrettyPrint() string {
    73→	out := new(strings.Builder)
    74→	sortedAddrs := slices.Collect(maps.Keys(t))
    75→	slices.SortFunc(sortedAddrs, common.Address.Cmp)
    76→
    77→	for _, addr := range sortedAddrs {
    78→		fmt.Fprintf(out, "%#x:", addr)
    79→		storage := t[addr]
    80→		sortedKeys := slices.Collect(maps.Keys(storage))
    81→		slices.SortFunc(sortedKeys, common.Hash.Cmp)
    82→		for _, key := range sortedKeys {
    83→			fmt.Fprintf(out, "  %X : %X\n", key, storage[key])
    84→		}
    85→	}

    35→type Storage map[common.Hash]common.Hash
    36→
    37→func (s Storage) Copy() Storage {
    38→	return maps.Clone(s)
    39→}
    40→
    41→// stateObject represents an Ethereum account which is being modified.
    42→//
    43→// The usage pattern is as follows:
    44→// - First you need to obtain a state object.
    45→// - Account values as well as storages can be accessed and modified through the object.
    46→// - Finally, call commit to return the changes of storage trie and update account data.
    47→type stateObject struct {
    48→	db       *StateDB
    49→	address  common.Address      // address of ethereum account
    50→	addrHash common.Hash         // hash of ethereum address of the account
    51→	origin   *types.StateAccount // Account original data without any change applied, nil means it was not existent
    52→	data     types.StateAccount  // Account data with all mutations applied in the scope of block
    53→
    54→	// Write caches.
    55→	trie Trie   // storage trie, which becomes non-nil on first access
    56→	code []byte // contract bytecode, which gets set when code is loaded
    57→
    58→	originStorage  Storage // Storage entries that have been accessed within the current block
    59→	dirtyStorage   Storage // Storage entries that have been modified within the current transaction
    60→	pendingStorage Storage // Storage entries that have been modified within the current block
    61→
    62→	// uncommittedStorage tracks a set of storage entries that have been modified
    63→	// but not yet committed since the "last commit operation", along with their
    64→	// original values before mutation.
    65→	//
    66→	// Specifically, the commit will be performed after each transaction before
    67→	// the byzantium fork, therefore the map is already reset at the transaction
    68→	// boundary; however post the byzantium fork, the commit will only be performed
    69→	// at the end of block, this set essentially tracks all the modifications
    70→	// made within the block.
    71→	uncommittedStorage Storage
    72→
    73→	// Cache flags.
    74→	dirtyCode bool // true if the code was updated
    75→
    76→	// Flag whether the account was marked as self-destructed. The self-destructed
    77→	// account is still accessible in the scope of same transaction.
    78→	selfDestructed bool
    79→
    80→	// This is an EIP-6780 flag indicating whether the object is eligible for
    81→	// self-destruct according to EIP-6780. The flag could be set either when
    82→	// the contract is just created within the current transaction, or when the
    83→	// object was previously existent and is being deployed as a contract within
    84→	// the current transaction.
    85→	newContract bool
    86→}
    87→
    88→// empty returns whether the account is considered empty.
    89→func (s *stateObject) empty() bool {
    90→	return s.data.Nonce == 0 && s.data.Balance.IsZero() && bytes.Equal(s.data.CodeHash, types.EmptyCodeHash.Bytes())
    91→}
    92→
    93→// newObject creates a state object.
    94→func newObject(db *StateDB, address common.Address, acct *types.StateAccount) *stateObject {
    95→	origin := acct
    96→	if acct == nil {
    97→		acct = types.NewEmptyStateAccount()
    98→	}
    99→	return &stateObject{
   100→		db:                 db,
   101→		address:            address,
   102→		addrHash:           crypto.Keccak256Hash(address[:]),
   103→		origin:             origin,
   104→		data:               *acct,
   105→		originStorage:      make(Storage),
   106→		dirtyStorage:       make(Storage),
   107→		pendingStorage:     make(Storage),
   108→		uncommittedStorage: make(Storage),
   109→	}
   110→}
   111→
   112→func (s *stateObject) markSelfdestructed() {
   113→	s.selfDestructed = true
   114→}
   115→
   116→func (s *stateObject) touch() {
   117→	s.db.journal.touchChange(s.address)
   118→}
   119→
   120→// getTrie returns the associated storage trie. The trie will be opened if it's
   121→// not loaded previously. An error will be returned if trie can't be loaded.
   122→//
   123→// If a new trie is opened, it will be cached within the state object to allow
   124→// subsequent reads to expand the same trie instead of reloading from disk.
   125→func (s *stateObject) getTrie() (Trie, error) {
   126→	if s.trie == nil {
   127→		// Assumes the primary account trie is already loaded
   128→		tr, err := s.db.db.OpenStorageTrie(s.db.originalRoot, s.address, s.data.Root, s.db.trie)
   129→		if err != nil {
   130→			return nil, err
   131→		}
   132→		s.trie = tr
   133→	}
   134→	return s.trie, nil
   135→}
   136→
   137→// getPrefetchedTrie returns the associated trie, as populated by the prefetcher
   138→// if it's available.
   139→//
   140→// Note, opposed to getTrie, this method will *NOT* blindly cache the resulting
   141→// trie in the state object. The caller might want to do that, but it's cleaner
   142→// to break the hidden interdependency between retrieving tries from the db or
   143→// from the prefetcher.
   144→func (s *stateObject) getPrefetchedTrie() Trie {
   145→	// If there's nothing to meaningfully return, let the user figure it out by
   146→	// pulling the trie from disk.
   147→	if (s.data.Root == types.EmptyRootHash && !s.db.db.TrieDB().IsVerkle()) || s.db.prefetcher == nil {
   148→		return nil
   149→	}
   150→	// Attempt to retrieve the trie from the prefetcher
   151→	return s.db.prefetcher.trie(s.addrHash, s.data.Root)
   152→}
   153→
   154→// GetState retrieves a value associated with the given storage key.
   155→func (s *stateObject) GetState(key common.Hash) common.Hash {
   156→	value, _ := s.getState(key)
   157→	return value
   158→}
   159→
   160→// getState retrieves a value associated with the given storage key, along with
   161→// its original value.
   162→func (s *stateObject) getState(key common.Hash) (common.Hash, common.Hash) {
   163→	origin := s.GetCommittedState(key)
   164→	value, dirty := s.dirtyStorage[key]
   165→	if dirty {
   166→		return value, origin
   167→	}
   168→	return origin, origin
   169→}
   170→
   171→// GetCommittedState retrieves the value associated with the specific key
   172→// without any mutations caused in the current execution.
   173→func (s *stateObject) GetCommittedState(key common.Hash) common.Hash {
   174→	// If we have a pending write or clean cached, return that
   175→	if value, pending := s.pendingStorage[key]; pending {
   176→		return value
   177→	}
   178→	if value, cached := s.originStorage[key]; cached {
   179→		return value
   180→	}
   181→	// If the object was destructed in *this* block (and potentially resurrected),
   182→	// the storage has been cleared out, and we should *not* consult the previous
   183→	// database about any storage values. The only possible alternatives are:
   184→	//   1) resurrect happened, and new slot values were set -- those should
   185→	//      have been handles via pendingStorage above.
   186→	//   2) we don't have new values, and can deliver empty response back
   187→	if _, destructed := s.db.stateObjectsDestruct[s.address]; destructed {
   188→		s.originStorage[key] = common.Hash{} // track the empty slot as origin value
   189→		return common.Hash{}
   190→	}
   191→	s.db.StorageLoaded++
   192→
   193→	start := time.Now()
   194→	value, err := s.db.reader.Storage(s.address, key)
   195→	if err != nil {
   196→		s.db.setError(err)
   197→		return common.Hash{}
   198→	}
   199→	s.db.StorageReads += time.Since(start)
   200→
   201→	// Schedule the resolved storage slots for prefetching if it's enabled.
   202→	if s.db.prefetcher != nil && s.data.Root != types.EmptyRootHash {
   203→		if err = s.db.prefetcher.prefetch(s.addrHash, s.origin.Root, s.address, nil, []common.Hash{key}, true); err != nil {
   204→			log.Error("Failed to prefetch storage slot", "addr", s.address, "key", key, "err", err)
   205→		}
   206→	}
   207→	s.originStorage[key] = value
   208→	return value
   209→}
   210→
   211→// SetState updates a value in account storage.
   212→// It returns the previous value
   213→func (s *stateObject) SetState(key, value common.Hash) common.Hash {
   214→	// If the new value is the same as old, don't set. Otherwise, track only the
   215→	// dirty changes, supporting reverting all of it back to no change.
   216→	prev, origin := s.getState(key)
   217→	if prev == value {
   218→		return prev
   219→	}
   220→	// New value is different, update and journal the change
   221→	s.db.journal.storageChange(s.address, key, prev, origin)
   222→	s.setState(key, value, origin)
   223→	return prev
   224→}
   225→
   226→// setState updates a value in account dirty storage. The dirtiness will be
   227→// removed if the value being set equals to the original value.
   228→func (s *stateObject) setState(key common.Hash, value common.Hash, origin common.Hash) {
   229→	// Storage slot is set back to its original value, undo the dirty marker
   230→	if value == origin {
   231→		delete(s.dirtyStorage, key)
   232→		return
   233→	}
   234→	s.dirtyStorage[key] = value
   235→}
   236→
   237→// finalise moves all dirty storage slots into the pending area to be hashed or
   238→// committed later. It is invoked at the end of every transaction.
   239→func (s *stateObject) finalise() {
   240→	slotsToPrefetch := make([]common.Hash, 0, len(s.dirtyStorage))
   241→	for key, value := range s.dirtyStorage {
   242→		if origin, exist := s.uncommittedStorage[key]; exist && origin == value {
   243→			// The slot is reverted to its original value, delete the entry
   244→			// to avoid thrashing the data structures.
   245→			delete(s.uncommittedStorage, key)
   246→		} else if exist {
   247→			// The slot is modified to another value and the slot has been
   248→			// tracked for commit, do nothing here.
   249→		} else {
   250→			// The slot is different from its original value and hasn't been
   251→			// tracked for commit yet.
   252→			s.uncommittedStorage[key] = s.GetCommittedState(key)
   253→			slotsToPrefetch = append(slotsToPrefetch, key) // Copy needed for closure
   254→		}
   255→		// Aggregate the dirty storage slots into the pending area. It might
   256→		// be possible that the value of tracked slot here is same with the
   257→		// one in originStorage (e.g. the slot was modified in tx_a and then
   258→		// modified back in tx_b). We can't blindly remove it from pending
   259→		// map as the dirty slot might have been committed already (before the
   260→		// byzantium fork) and entry is necessary to modify the value back.
   261→		s.pendingStorage[key] = value
   262→	}
   263→	if s.db.prefetcher != nil && len(slotsToPrefetch) > 0 && s.data.Root != types.EmptyRootHash {
   264→		if err := s.db.prefetcher.prefetch(s.addrHash, s.data.Root, s.address, nil, slotsToPrefetch, false); err != nil {
   265→			log.Error("Failed to prefetch slots", "addr", s.address, "slots", len(slotsToPrefetch), "err", err)
   266→		}
   267→	}
   268→	if len(s.dirtyStorage) > 0 {
   269→		s.dirtyStorage = make(Storage)
   270→	}
   271→	// Revoke the flag at the end of the transaction. It finalizes the status
   272→	// of the newly-created object as it's no longer eligible for self-destruct
   273→	// by EIP-6780. For non-newly-created objects, it's a no-op.
   274→	s.newContract = false
   275→}
   276→
   277→// updateTrie is responsible for persisting cached storage changes into the
   278→// object's storage trie. In case the storage trie is not yet loaded, this
   279→// function will load the trie automatically. If any issues arise during the
   280→// loading or updating of the trie, an error will be returned. Furthermore,
   281→// this function will return the mutated storage trie, or nil if there is no
   282→// storage change at all.
   283→//
   284→// It assumes all the dirty storage slots have been finalized before.
   285→func (s *stateObject) updateTrie() (Trie, error) {
   286→	// Short circuit if nothing was accessed, don't trigger a prefetcher warning
   287→	if len(s.uncommittedStorage) == 0 {
   288→		// Nothing was written, so we could stop early. Unless we have both reads
   289→		// and witness collection enabled, in which case we need to fetch the trie.
   290→		if s.db.witness == nil || len(s.originStorage) == 0 {
   291→			return s.trie, nil
   292→		}
   293→	}

   295→	// block until all prefetch tasks are done, which are needed for witnesses even

    68→// StateDB structs within the ethereum protocol are used to store anything
    69→// within the merkle trie. StateDBs take care of caching and storing
    70→// nested states. It's the general query interface to retrieve:
    71→//
    72→// * Contracts
    73→// * Accounts
    74→//
    75→// Once the state is committed, tries cached in stateDB (including account
    76→// trie, storage tries) will no longer be functional. A new state instance
    77→// must be created with new root and updated database for accessing post-
    78→// commit states.
    79→type StateDB struct {
    80→	db         Database
    81→	prefetcher *triePrefetcher
    82→	reader     Reader
    83→	trie       Trie // it's resolved on first access
    84→
    85→	// originalRoot is the pre-state root, before any changes were made.
    86→	// It will be updated when the Commit is called.
    87→	originalRoot common.Hash
    88→
    89→	// This map holds 'live' objects, which will get modified while
    90→	// processing a state transition.
    91→	stateObjects map[common.Address]*stateObject
    92→
    93→	// This map holds 'deleted' objects. An object with the same address
    94→	// might also occur in the 'stateObjects' map due to account
    95→	// resurrection. The account value is tracked as the original value
    96→	// before the transition. This map is populated at the transaction
    97→	// boundaries.
    98→	stateObjectsDestruct map[common.Address]*stateObject
    99→
   100→	// This map tracks the account mutations that occurred during the
   101→	// transition. Uncommitted mutations belonging to the same account
   102→	// can be merged into a single one which is equivalent from database's
   103→	// perspective. This map is populated at the transaction boundaries.
   104→	mutations map[common.Address]*mutation
   105→
   106→	// DB error.
   107→	// State objects are used by the consensus core and VM which are
   108→	// unable to deal with database-level errors. Any error that occurs
   109→	// during a database read is memoized here and will eventually be
   110→	// returned by StateDB.Commit. Notably, this error is also shared
   111→	// by all cached state objects in case the database failure occurs
   112→	// when accessing state of accounts.
   113→	dbErr error
   114→
   115→	// The refund counter, also used by state transitioning.
   116→	refund uint64
   117→
   118→	// The tx context and all occurred logs in the scope of transaction.
   119→	thash   common.Hash
   120→	txIndex int
   121→	logs    map[common.Hash][]*types.Log
   122→	logSize uint
   123→
   124→	// Preimages occurred seen by VM in the scope of block.
   125→	preimages map[common.Hash][]byte
   126→
   127→	// Per-transaction access list
   128→	accessList   *accessList
   129→	accessEvents *AccessEvents
   130→
   131→	// Transient storage
   132→	transientStorage transientStorage
   133→
   134→	// Journal of state modifications. This is the backbone of
   135→	// Snapshot and RevertToSnapshot.
   136→	journal *journal
   137→
   138→	// State witness if cross validation is needed
   139→	witness      *stateless.Witness
   140→	witnessStats *stateless.WitnessStats
   141→
   142→	// Measurements gathered during execution for debugging purposes
   143→	AccountReads    time.Duration
   144→	AccountHashes   time.Duration
   145→	AccountUpdates  time.Duration
   146→	AccountCommits  time.Duration
   147→	StorageReads    time.Duration
   148→	StorageUpdates  time.Duration
   149→	StorageCommits  time.Duration
   150→	SnapshotCommits time.Duration
   151→	TrieDBCommits   time.Duration
   152→
   153→	AccountLoaded  int          // Number of accounts retrieved from the database during the state transition
   154→	AccountUpdated int          // Number of accounts updated during the state transition
   155→	AccountDeleted int          // Number of accounts deleted during the state transition
   156→	StorageLoaded  int          // Number of storage slots retrieved from the database during the state transition
   157→	StorageUpdated atomic.Int64 // Number of storage slots updated during the state transition
   158→	StorageDeleted atomic.Int64 // Number of storage slots deleted during the state transition
   159→}

   161→// New creates a new state from a given trie.
   162→func New(root common.Hash, db Database) (*StateDB, error) {
   163→	reader, err := db.Reader(root)
   164→	if err != nil {
   165→		return nil, err
   166→	}
   167→	return NewWithReader(root, db, reader)
   168→}
   169→
   170→// NewWithReader creates a new state for the specified state root. Unlike New,
   171→// this function accepts an additional Reader which is bound to the given root.
   172→func NewWithReader(root common.Hash, db Database, reader Reader) (*StateDB, error) {
   173→	sdb := &StateDB{
   174→		db:                   db,
   175→		originalRoot:         root,
   176→		reader:               reader,
   177→		stateObjects:         make(map[common.Address]*stateObject),
   178→		stateObjectsDestruct: make(map[common.Address]*stateObject),
   179→		mutations:            make(map[common.Address]*mutation),
   180→		logs:                 make(map[common.Hash][]*types.Log),
   181→		preimages:            make(map[common.Hash][]byte),
   182→		journal:              newJournal(),
   183→		accessList:           newAccessList(),
   184→		transientStorage:     newTransientStorage(),
   185→	}
   186→	if db.TrieDB().IsVerkle() {
   187→		sdb.accessEvents = NewAccessEvents(db.PointCache())
   188→	}
   189→	return sdb, nil
   190→}

   192→// StartPrefetcher initializes a new trie prefetcher to pull in nodes from the
   193→// state trie concurrently while the state is mutated so that when we reach the
   194→// commit phase, most of the needed data is already hot.
   195→func (s *StateDB) StartPrefetcher(namespace string, witness *stateless.Witness, witnessStats *stateless.WitnessStats) {
   196→	// Terminate any previously running prefetcher
   197→	s.StopPrefetcher()
   198→
   199→	// Enable witness collection if requested
   200→	s.witness = witness
   201→	s.witnessStats = witnessStats
   202→
   203→	// With the switch to the Proof-of-Stake consensus algorithm, block production
   204→	// rewards are now handled at the consensus layer. Consequently, a block may
   205→	// have no state transitions if it contains no transactions and no withdrawals.
   206→	// In such cases, the account trie won't be scheduled for prefetching, leading
   207→	// to unnecessary error logs.
   208→	//
   209→	// To prevent this, the account trie is always scheduled for prefetching once
   210→	// the prefetcher is constructed. For more details, see:
   211→	// https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/29880
   212→	s.prefetcher = newTriePrefetcher(s.db, s.originalRoot, namespace, witness == nil)
   213→	if err := s.prefetcher.prefetch(common.Hash{}, s.originalRoot, common.Address{}, nil, nil, false); err != nil {
   214→		log.Error("Failed to prefetch account trie", "root", s.originalRoot, "err", err)
   215→	}
   216→}

   218→// StopPrefetcher terminates a running prefetcher and reports any leftover stats
   219→// from the gathered metrics.
   220→func (s *StateDB) StopPrefetcher() {
   221→	if s.prefetcher != nil {
   222→		s.prefetcher.terminate(false)
   223→		s.prefetcher.report()
   224→		s.prefetcher = nil
   225→	}
   226→}

   240→func (s *StateDB) AddLog(log *types.Log) {
   241→	s.journal.logChange(s.thash)
   242→
   243→	log.TxHash = s.thash
   244→	log.TxIndex = uint(s.txIndex)
   245→	log.Index = s.logSize
   246→	s.logs[s.thash] = append(s.logs[s.thash], log)
   247→	s.logSize++
   248→}
   249→
   250→// GetLogs returns the logs matching the specified transaction hash, and annotates
   251→// them with the given blockNumber and blockHash.
   252→func (s *StateDB) GetLogs(hash common.Hash, blockNumber uint64, blockHash common.Hash, blockTime uint64) []*types.Log {
   253→	logs := s.logs[hash]
   254→	for _, l := range logs {
   255→		l.BlockNumber = blockNumber
   256→		l.BlockHash = blockHash
   257→		l.BlockTimestamp = blockTime
   258→	}
   259→	return logs
   260→}
   261→
   262→func (s *StateDB) Logs() []*types.Log {
   263→	logs := make([]*types.Log, 0, s.logSize)
   264→	for _, lgs := range s.logs {
   265→		logs = append(logs, lgs...)
   266→	}
   267→	return logs
   268→}

   271→func (s *StateDB) AddPreimage(hash common.Hash, preimage []byte) {
   272→	if _, ok := s.preimages[hash]; !ok {
   273→		s.preimages[hash] = slices.Clone(preimage)
   274→	}
   275→}

   277→// Preimages returns a list of SHA3 preimages that have been submitted.
   278→func (s *StateDB) Preimages() map[common.Hash][]byte {

   282→// AddRefund adds gas to the refund counter
   283→func (s *StateDB) AddRefund(gas uint64) {
   284→	s.journal.refundChange(s.refund)
   285→	s.refund += gas
   286→}
   287→
   288→// SubRefund removes gas from the refund counter.
   289→// This method will panic if the refund counter goes below zero
   290→func (s *StateDB) SubRefund(gas uint64) {
   291→	s.journal.refundChange(s.refund)
   292→	if gas > s.refund {
   293→		panic(fmt.Sprintf("Refund counter below zero (gas: %d > refund: %d)", gas, s.refund))
   294→	}
   295→	s.refund -= gas
   296→}

   435→// SubBalance subtracts amount from the account associated with addr.
   436→func (s *StateDB) SubBalance(addr common.Address, amount *uint256.Int, reason tracing.BalanceChangeReason) uint256.Int {
   437→	stateObject := s.getOrNewStateObject(addr)
   438→	if stateObject == nil {
   439→		return uint256.Int{}
   440→	}
   441→	if amount.IsZero() {
   442→		return *(stateObject.Balance())

   476→// SetStorage replaces the entire storage for the specified account with given
   477→// storage. This function should only be used for debugging and the mutations
   478→// must be discarded afterwards.
   479→func (s *StateDB) SetStorage(addr common.Address, storage map[common.Hash]common.Hash) {
   480→	// SetStorage needs to wipe the existing storage. We achieve this by marking
   481→	// the account as self-destructed in this block. The effect is that storage
   482→	// lookups will not hit the disk, as it is assumed that the disk data belongs
   483→	// to a previous incarnation of the object.
   484→	//
   485→	// TODO (rjl493456442): This function should only be supported by 'unwritable'
   486→	// state, and all mutations made should be discarded afterward.
   487→	obj := s.getStateObject(addr)
   488→	if obj != nil {
   489→		if _, ok := s.stateObjectsDestruct[addr]; !ok {
   490→			s.stateObjectsDestruct[addr] = obj
   491→		}
   492→	}
   493→	newObj := s.createObject(addr)
   494→	for k, v := range storage {
   495→		newObj.SetState(k, v)
   496→	}
   497→	// Inherit the metadata of original object if it was existent
   498→	if obj != nil {
   499→		newObj.SetCode(common.BytesToHash(obj.CodeHash()), obj.code)
   500→		newObj.SetNonce(obj.Nonce())
   501→		newObj.SetBalance(obj.Balance())

   505→// SelfDestruct marks the given account as selfdestructed.
   506→// This clears the account balance.
   507→//
   508→// The account's state object is still available until the state is committed,
   509→// getStateObject will return a non-nil account after SelfDestruct.
   510→func (s *StateDB) SelfDestruct(addr common.Address) uint256.Int {
   511→	stateObject := s.getStateObject(addr)
   512→	var prevBalance uint256.Int
   513→	if stateObject == nil {
   514→		return prevBalance
   515→	}
   516→	prevBalance = *(stateObject.Balance())
   517→	// Regardless of whether it is already destructed or not, we do have to
   518→	// journal the balance-change, if we set it to zero here.
   519→	if !stateObject.Balance().IsZero() {
   520→		stateObject.SetBalance(new(uint256.Int))
   521→	}
   522→	// If it is already marked as self-destructed, we do not need to add it
   523→	// for journalling a second time.
   524→	if !stateObject.selfDestructed {
   525→		s.journal.destruct(addr)
   526→		stateObject.markSelfdestructed()
   527→	}
   528→	return prevBalance
   529→}

   531→func (s *StateDB) SelfDestruct6780(addr common.Address) (uint256.Int, bool) {
   532→	stateObject := s.getStateObject(addr)
   533→	if stateObject == nil {
   534→		return uint256.Int{}, false
   535→	}
   536→	if stateObject.newContract {
   537→		return s.SelfDestruct(addr), true
   538→	}
   539→	return *(stateObject.Balance()), false
   540→}

   587→// getStateObject retrieves a state object given by the address, returning nil if
   588→// the object is not found or was deleted in this execution context.
   589→func (s *StateDB) getStateObject(addr common.Address) *stateObject {
   590→	// Prefer live objects if any is available
   591→	if obj := s.stateObjects[addr]; obj != nil {
   592→		return obj
   593→	}
   594→	// Short circuit if the account is already destructed in this block.
   595→	if _, ok := s.stateObjectsDestruct[addr]; ok {
   596→		return nil
   597→	}
   598→	s.AccountLoaded++
   599→
   600→	start := time.Now()
   601→	acct, err := s.reader.Account(addr)
   602→	if err != nil {
   603→		s.setError(fmt.Errorf("getStateObject (%x) error: %w", addr.Bytes(), err))
   604→		return nil
   605→	}
   606→	s.AccountReads += time.Since(start)
   607→
   608→	// Short circuit if the account is not found
   609→	if acct == nil {
   610→		return nil
   611→	}
   612→	// Schedule the resolved account for prefetching if it's enabled.
   613→	if s.prefetcher != nil {
   614→		if err = s.prefetcher.prefetch(common.Hash{}, s.originalRoot, common.Address{}, []common.Address{addr}, nil, true); err != nil {
   615→			log.Error("Failed to prefetch account", "addr", addr, "err", err)
   616→		}
   617→	}
   618→	// Insert into the live set
   619→	obj := newObject(s, addr, acct)
   620→	s.setStateObject(obj)
   621→	return obj
   622→}

   667→// Copy creates a deep, independent copy of the state.
   668→// Snapshots of the copied state cannot be applied to the copy.
   669→func (s *StateDB) Copy() *StateDB {
   670→	// Copy all the basic fields, initialize the memory ones
   671→	state := &StateDB{
   672→		db:                   s.db,
   673→		reader:               s.reader,
   674→		originalRoot:         s.originalRoot,
   675→		stateObjects:         make(map[common.Address]*stateObject, len(s.stateObjects)),
   676→		stateObjectsDestruct: make(map[common.Address]*stateObject, len(s.stateObjectsDestruct)),
   677→		mutations:            make(map[common.Address]*mutation, len(s.mutations)),
   678→		dbErr:                s.dbErr,
   679→		refund:               s.refund,
   680→		thash:                s.thash,
   681→		txIndex:              s.txIndex,
   682→		logs:                 make(map[common.Hash][]*types.Log, len(s.logs)),
   683→		logSize:              s.logSize,
   684→		preimages:            maps.Clone(s.preimages),
   685→
   686→		// Do we need to copy the access list and transient storage?
   687→		// In practice: No. At the start of a transaction, these two lists are empty.
   688→		// In practice, we only ever copy state _between_ transactions/blocks, never
   689→		// in the middle of a transaction. However, it doesn't cost us much to copy
   690→		// empty lists, so we do it anyway to not blow up if we ever decide copy them
   691→		// in the middle of a transaction.
   692→		accessList:       s.accessList.Copy(),
   693→		transientStorage: s.transientStorage.Copy(),
   694→		journal:          s.journal.copy(),
   695→	}
   696→	if s.trie != nil {
   697→		state.trie = mustCopyTrie(s.trie)
   698→	}
   699→	if s.witness != nil {
   700→		state.witness = s.witness.Copy()
   701→	}
   702→	if s.accessEvents != nil {
   703→		state.accessEvents = s.accessEvents.Copy()
   704→	}
   705→	// Deep copy cached state objects.
   706→	for addr, obj := range s.stateObjects {
   707→		state.stateObjects[addr] = obj.deepCopy(state)
   708→	}
   709→	// Deep copy destructed state objects.
   710→	for addr, obj := range s.stateObjectsDestruct {
   711→		state.stateObjectsDestruct[addr] = obj.deepCopy(state)
   712→	}
   713→	// Deep copy the object state markers.
   714→	for addr, op := range s.mutations {
   715→		state.mutations[addr] = op.copy()
   716→	}
   717→	// Deep copy the logs occurred in the scope of block
   718→	for hash, logs := range s.logs {
   719→		cpy := make([]*types.Log, len(logs))
   720→		for i, l := range logs {
   721→			cpy[i] = new(types.Log)
   722→			*cpy[i] = *l
   723→		}
   724→		state.logs[hash] = cpy
   725→	}
   726→	return state
   727→}

   744→// Finalise finalises the state by removing the destructed objects and clears
   745→// the journal as well as the refunds. Finalise, however, will not push any updates
   746→// into the tries just yet. Only IntermediateRoot or Commit will do that.
   747→func (s *StateDB) Finalise(deleteEmptyObjects bool) {
   748→	addressesToPrefetch := make([]common.Address, 0, len(s.journal.dirties))
   749→	for addr := range s.journal.dirties {
   750→		obj, exist := s.stateObjects[addr]
   751→		if !exist {
   752→			// ripeMD is 'touched' at block 1714175, in tx 0x1237f737031e40bcde4a8b7e717b2d15e3ecadfe49bb1bbc71ee9deb09c6fcf2
   753→			// That tx goes out of gas, and although the notion of 'touched' does not exist there, the
   754→			// touch-event will still be recorded in the journal. Since ripeMD is a special snowflake,
   755→			// it will persist in the journal even though the journal is reverted. In this special circumstance,
   756→			// it may exist in `s.journal.dirties` but not in `s.stateObjects`.
   757→			// Thus, we can safely ignore it here
   758→			continue
   759→		}
   760→		if obj.selfDestructed || (deleteEmptyObjects && obj.empty()) {
   761→			delete(s.stateObjects, obj.address)
   762→			s.markDelete(addr)
   763→			// We need to maintain account deletions explicitly (will remain
   764→			// set indefinitely). Note only the first occurred self-destruct
   765→			// event is tracked.
   766→			if _, ok := s.stateObjectsDestruct[obj.address]; !ok {
   767→				s.stateObjectsDestruct[obj.address] = obj
   768→			}
   769→		} else {
   770→			obj.finalise()
   771→			s.markUpdate(addr)
   772→		}
   773→		// At this point, also ship the address off to the precacher. The precacher
   774→		// will start loading tries, and when the change is eventually committed,
   775→		// the commit-phase will be a lot faster
   776→		addressesToPrefetch = append(addressesToPrefetch, addr) // Copy needed for closure
   777→	}
   778→	if s.prefetcher != nil && len(addressesToPrefetch) > 0 {
   779→		if err := s.prefetcher.prefetch(common.Hash{}, s.originalRoot, common.Address{}, addressesToPrefetch, nil, false); err != nil {
   780→			log.Error("Failed to prefetch addresses", "addresses", len(addressesToPrefetch), "err", err)
   781→		}
   782→	}
   783→	// Invalidate journal because reverting across transactions is not allowed.
   784→	s.clearJournalAndRefund()
   785→}

   787→// IntermediateRoot computes the current root hash of the state trie.
   788→// It is called in between transactions to get the root hash that
   789→// goes into transaction receipts.
   790→func (s *StateDB) IntermediateRoot(deleteEmptyObjects bool) common.Hash {
   791→	// Finalise all the dirty storage states and write them into the tries
   792→	s.Finalise(deleteEmptyObjects)
   793→
   794→	// Initialize the trie if it's not constructed yet. If the prefetch
   795→	// is enabled, the trie constructed below will be replaced by the
   796→	// prefetched one.
   797→	//
   798→	// This operation must be done before state object storage hashing,
   799→	// as it assumes the main trie is already loaded.
   800→	if s.trie == nil {
   801→		tr, err := s.db.OpenTrie(s.originalRoot)
   802→		if err != nil {
   803→			s.setError(err)
   804→			return common.Hash{}
   805→		}
   806→		s.trie = tr
   807→	}
   808→	// If there was a trie prefetcher operating, terminate it async so that the
   809→	// individual storage tries can be updated as soon as the disk load finishes.
   810→	if s.prefetcher != nil {
   811→		s.prefetcher.terminate(true)
   812→		defer func() {
   813→			s.prefetcher.report()
   814→			s.prefetcher = nil // Pre-byzantium, unset any used up prefetcher
   815→		}()
   816→	}
   817→	// Process all storage updates concurrently. The state object update root
   818→	// method will internally call a blocking trie fetch from the prefetcher,
   819→	// so there's no need to explicitly wait for the prefetchers to finish.
   820→	var (
   821→		start   = time.Now()
   822→		workers errgroup.Group
   823→	)
   824→	if s.db.TrieDB().IsVerkle() {
   825→		// Whilst MPT storage tries are independent, Verkle has one single trie
   826→		// for all the accounts and all the storage slots merged together. The
   827→		// former can thus be simply parallelized, but updating the latter will
   828→		// need concurrency support within the trie itself. That's a TODO for a
   829→		// later time.
   830→		workers.SetLimit(1)
   831→	}
   832→	for addr, op := range s.mutations {
   833→		if op.applied || op.isDelete() {
   834→			continue
   835→		}
   836→		obj := s.stateObjects[addr] // closure for the task runner below
   837→		workers.Go(func() error {
   838→			if s.db.TrieDB().IsVerkle() {
   839→				obj.updateTrie()
   840→			} else {
   841→				obj.updateRoot()
   842→
   843→				// If witness building is enabled and the state object has a trie,
   844→				// gather the witnesses for its specific storage trie
   845→				if s.witness != nil && obj.trie != nil {
   846→					s.witness.AddState(obj.trie.Witness())
   847→				}
   848→			}
   849→			return nil
   850→		})
   851→	}
   852→	// If witness building is enabled, gather all the read-only accesses.
   853→	// Skip witness collection in Verkle mode, they will be gathered
   854→	// together at the end.
   855→	if s.witness != nil && !s.db.TrieDB().IsVerkle() {
   856→		// Pull in anything that has been accessed before destruction
   857→		for _, obj := range s.stateObjectsDestruct {
   858→			// Skip any objects that haven't touched their storage
   859→			if len(obj.originStorage) == 0 {
   860→				continue
   861→			}
   862→			if trie := obj.getPrefetchedTrie(); trie != nil {
   863→				witness := trie.Witness()
   864→				s.witness.AddState(witness)
   865→				if s.witnessStats != nil {
   866→					s.witnessStats.Add(witness, obj.addrHash)
   867→				}
   868→			} else if obj.trie != nil {
   869→				witness := obj.trie.Witness()
   870→				s.witness.AddState(witness)
   871→				if s.witnessStats != nil {
   872→					s.witnessStats.Add(witness, obj.addrHash)
   873→				}
   874→			}
   875→		}
   876→		// Pull in only-read and non-destructed trie witnesses
   877→		for _, obj := range s.stateObjects {
   878→			// Skip any objects that have been updated
   879→			if _, ok := s.mutations[obj.address]; ok {
   880→				continue
   881→			}
   882→			// Skip any objects that haven't touched their storage
   883→			if len(obj.originStorage) == 0 {
   884→				continue
   885→			}
   886→			if trie := obj.getPrefetchedTrie(); trie != nil {
   887→				witness := trie.Witness()
   888→				s.witness.AddState(witness)
   889→				if s.witnessStats != nil {
   890→					s.witnessStats.Add(witness, obj.addrHash)
   891→				}
   892→			} else if obj.trie != nil {
   893→				witness := obj.trie.Witness()
   894→				s.witness.AddState(witness)
   895→				if s.witnessStats != nil {
   896→					s.witnessStats.Add(witness, obj.addrHash)
   897→				}
   898→			}
   899→		}
   900→	}
   901→	workers.Wait()
   902→	s.StorageUpdates += time.Since(start)
   903→
   904→	// Now we're about to start to write changes to the trie. The trie is so far
   905→	// _untouched_. We can check with the prefetcher, if it can give us a trie
   906→	// which has the same root, but also has some content loaded into it.
   907→	//
   908→	// Don't check prefetcher if verkle trie has been used. In the context of verkle,
   909→	// only a single trie is used for state hashing. Replacing a non-nil verkle tree
   910→	// here could result in losing uncommitted changes from storage.
   911→	start = time.Now()
   912→	if s.prefetcher != nil {
   913→		if trie := s.prefetcher.trie(common.Hash{}, s.originalRoot); trie == nil {
   914→			log.Error("Failed to retrieve account pre-fetcher trie")
   915→		} else {
   916→			s.trie = trie
   917→		}
   918→	}
   919→	// Perform updates before deletions.  This prevents resolution of unnecessary trie nodes
   920→	// in circumstances similar to the following:
   921→	//
   922→	// Consider nodes `A` and `B` who share the same full node parent `P` and have no other siblings.
   923→	// During the execution of a block:
   924→	// - `A` self-destructs,
   925→	// - `C` is created, and also shares the parent `P`.
   926→	// If the self-destruct is handled first, then `P` would be left with only one child, thus collapsed
   927→	// into a shortnode. This requires `B` to be resolved from disk.
   928→	// Whereas if the created node is handled first, then the collapse is avoided, and `B` is not resolved.
   929→	var (
   930→		usedAddrs    []common.Address
   931→		deletedAddrs []common.Address
   932→	)
   933→	for addr, op := range s.mutations {
   934→		if op.applied {
   935→			continue
   936→		}
   937→		op.applied = true
   938→
   939→		if op.isDelete() {
   940→			deletedAddrs = append(deletedAddrs, addr)
   941→		} else {
   942→			s.updateStateObject(s.stateObjects[addr])
   943→			s.AccountUpdated += 1
   944→		}
   945→		usedAddrs = append(usedAddrs, addr) // Copy needed for closure
   946→	}
   947→	for _, deletedAddr := range deletedAddrs {
   948→		s.deleteStateObject(deletedAddr)
   949→		s.AccountDeleted += 1
   950→	}
   951→	s.AccountUpdates += time.Since(start)
   952→
   953→	if s.prefetcher != nil {
   954→		s.prefetcher.used(common.Hash{}, s.originalRoot, usedAddrs, nil)
   955→	}
   956→	// Track the amount of time wasted on hashing the account trie
   957→	defer func(start time.Time) { s.AccountHashes += time.Since(start) }(time.Now())
   958→
   959→	hash := s.trie.Hash()
   960→
   961→	// If witness building is enabled, gather the account trie witness
   962→	if s.witness != nil {
   963→		witness := s.trie.Witness()
   964→		s.witness.AddState(witness)
   965→		if s.witnessStats != nil {
   966→			s.witnessStats.Add(witness, common.Hash{})
   967→		}
   968→	}
   969→	return hash
   970→}

   984→
   985→// fastDeleteStorage is the function that efficiently deletes the storage trie
   986→// of a specific account. It leverages the associated state snapshot for fast
   987→// storage iteration and constructs trie node deletion markers by creating
   988→// stack trie with iterated slots.
   989→func (s *StateDB) fastDeleteStorage(snaps *snapshot.Tree, addrHash common.Hash, root common.Hash) (map[common.Hash][]byte, map[common.Hash][]byte, *trienode.NodeSet, error) {
   990→	iter, err := snaps.StorageIterator(s.originalRoot, addrHash, common.Hash{})
   991→	if err != nil {
   992→		return nil, nil, nil, err
   993→	}
   994→	defer iter.Release()
   995→
   996→	var (
   997→		nodes          = trienode.NewNodeSet(addrHash) // the set for trie node mutations (value is nil)
   998→		storages       = make(map[common.Hash][]byte)  // the set for storage mutations (value is nil)
   999→		storageOrigins = make(map[common.Hash][]byte)  // the set for tracking the original value of slot
  1000→	)
  1001→	stack := trie.NewStackTrie(func(path []byte, hash common.Hash, blob []byte) {
  1002→		nodes.AddNode(path, trienode.NewDeletedWithPrev(blob))
  1003→	})
  1004→	for iter.Next() {
  1005→		slot := common.CopyBytes(iter.Slot())
  1006→		if err := iter.Error(); err != nil { // error might occur after Slot function
  1007→			return nil, nil, nil, err
  1008→		}
  1009→		key := iter.Hash()
  1010→		storages[key] = nil
  1011→		storageOrigins[key] = slot
  1012→
  1013→		if err := stack.Update(key.Bytes(), slot); err != nil {
  1014→			return nil, nil, nil, err
  1015→		}
  1016→	}
  1017→	if err := iter.Error(); err != nil { // error might occur during iteration
  1018→		return nil, nil, nil, err
  1019→	}
  1020→	if stack.Hash() != root {
  1021→		return nil, nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("snapshot is not matched, exp %x, got %x", root, stack.Hash())
  1022→	}
  1023→	return storages, storageOrigins, nodes, nil
  1024→}

  1026→// slowDeleteStorage serves as a less-efficient alternative to "fastDeleteStorage,"
  1027→// employed when the associated state snapshot is not available. It iterates the
  1028→// storage slots along with all internal trie nodes via trie directly.
  1029→func (s *StateDB) slowDeleteStorage(addr common.Address, addrHash common.Hash, root common.Hash) (map[common.Hash][]byte, map[common.Hash][]byte, *trienode.NodeSet, error) {
  1030→	tr, err := s.db.OpenStorageTrie(s.originalRoot, addr, root, s.trie)
  1031→	if err != nil {
  1032→		return nil, nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to open storage trie, err: %w", err)
  1033→	}
  1034→	it, err := tr.NodeIterator(nil)
  1035→	if err != nil {
  1036→		return nil, nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to open storage iterator, err: %w", err)
  1037→	}
  1038→	var (
  1039→		nodes          = trienode.NewNodeSet(addrHash) // the set for trie node mutations (value is nil)
  1040→		storages       = make(map[common.Hash][]byte)  // the set for storage mutations (value is nil)
  1041→		storageOrigins = make(map[common.Hash][]byte)  // the set for tracking the original value of slot
  1042→	)
  1043→	for it.Next(true) {
  1044→		if it.Leaf() {
  1045→			key := common.BytesToHash(it.LeafKey())
  1046→			storages[key] = nil
  1047→			storageOrigins[key] = common.CopyBytes(it.LeafBlob())
  1048→			continue
  1049→		}
  1050→		if it.Hash() == (common.Hash{}) {
  1051→			continue
  1052→		}
  1053→		nodes.AddNode(it.Path(), trienode.NewDeletedWithPrev(it.NodeBlob()))
  1054→	}
  1055→	if err := it.Error(); err != nil {
  1056→		return nil, nil, nil, err
  1057→	}
  1058→	return storages, storageOrigins, nodes, nil
  1059→}

  1061→// deleteStorage is designed to delete the storage trie of a designated account.
  1062→// The function will make an attempt to utilize an efficient strategy if the
  1063→// associated state snapshot is reachable; otherwise, it will resort to a less
  1064→// efficient approach.
  1065→func (s *StateDB) deleteStorage(addr common.Address, addrHash common.Hash, root common.Hash) (map[common.Hash][]byte, map[common.Hash][]byte, *trienode.NodeSet, error) {
  1066→	var (
  1067→		err            error
  1068→		nodes          *trienode.NodeSet      // the set for trie node mutations (value is nil)
  1069→		storages       map[common.Hash][]byte // the set for storage mutations (value is nil)
  1070→		storageOrigins map[common.Hash][]byte // the set for tracking the original value of slot
  1071→	)
  1072→	// The fast approach can be failed if the snapshot is not fully
  1073→	// generated, or it's internally corrupted. Fallback to the slow
  1074→	// one just in case.
  1075→	snaps := s.db.Snapshot()
  1076→	if snaps != nil {
  1077→		storages, storageOrigins, nodes, err = s.fastDeleteStorage(snaps, addrHash, root)
  1078→	}
  1079→	if snaps == nil || err != nil {
  1080→		storages, storageOrigins, nodes, err = s.slowDeleteStorage(addr, addrHash, root)
  1081→	}
  1082→	if err != nil {
  1083→		return nil, nil, nil, err
  1084→	}
  1085→	return storages, storageOrigins, nodes, nil
  1086→}
